item.content:encoded:
The ONE Campaign is inviting passionate individuals in Canada to apply for the ONE Canada Global Activists 2026–2027 cohort. This volunteer opportunity is designed for people who want to advocate for stronger investments that create economic opportunities, improve health outcomes and support a healthier future across Africa.

The program offers participants the chance to strengthen their advocacy, communications and leadership skills while becoming part of a wider international network of activists working to advance global justice.

Applications for the 2026–2027 cohort are open to eligible residents of Canada, with the program scheduled to run from October 2026 to October 2027.

About the ONE Canada Global Activists Program

The ONE Global Activists program brings together people who are passionate about tackling global inequality and advocating for policies and investments that can improve lives, particularly across Africa.

As a Global Activist in Canada, participants will have opportunities to learn about advocacy, Canadian and international politics, development finance and media engagement. They will also be supported in taking meaningful action within their communities and engaging decision-makers on issues connected to ONE’s advocacy priorities.

The program is particularly suited to individuals who want to turn their interest in global development into practical advocacy experience.

What Will Global Activists Do?

Selected participants will become part of a network of advocates working to support ONE’s campaigns and public advocacy efforts.

Depending on their interests and activities, Global Activists may have opportunities to:

  • Participate in advocacy campaigns focused on global development and Africa.
  • Engage with elected officials and other decision-makers.
  • Represent ONE at relevant events and activities.
  • Take part in community-based advocacy actions.
  • Help raise awareness of issues affecting global development and economic opportunity.
  • Use communications and social media to mobilize people around advocacy campaigns.
  • Connect with other activists in Canada and the wider ONE Global Activists network.
  • Contribute creative ideas and actions that support ONE’s advocacy priorities.

The program therefore combines learning, networking and practical advocacy experience rather than being limited to classroom-style training.

APPLY HERE.

Training and Skills Development

One of the major benefits of joining the ONE Canada Global Activists program is access to training designed to help participants become more effective advocates.

Training will cover areas such as:

Advocacy

Participants can develop practical knowledge of how advocacy campaigns are designed and implemented, including how individuals and communities can influence public policy.

Canadian and Global Politics

The program provides opportunities to better understand Canadian politics and the broader international political environment in which global development decisions are made.

Media and Communications

Activists can strengthen their ability to communicate important issues through media, public speaking, social media and other communication channels.

Development Finance

Participants interested in international development can develop a stronger understanding of development finance and the investments required to support economic opportunities and healthier lives in Africa.

These skills can be useful for individuals interested in communications, international development, nonprofit work, advocacy, public policy, community organizing and social impact.

Networking Opportunities

Joining the program also means becoming part of a broader community.

Global Activists in Canada will have the opportunity to connect with other activists across Canada as well as members of the ONE Global Activists network in:

  • Canada
  • Europe
  • Africa
  • The United States

This international network can provide opportunities to exchange ideas, learn from other advocates and build connections with people working on similar global issues.

Opportunities to Meet Elected Officials

Participants may have opportunities to represent ONE and engage directly with elected officials.

This can provide valuable practical exposure to political advocacy and help participants understand how campaign messages can be communicated to policymakers.

For people interested in public policy, government relations, international development, communications or political advocacy, this can be an important learning experience.

Community Action and Advocacy Support

Global Activists will receive dedicated support to develop and carry out creative community actions that contribute to ONE’s advocacy work.

This means participants are not expected to work completely independently. The program provides support as activists develop activities designed to raise awareness, engage communities and encourage action around important global issues.

Key ONE Campaign Issues

Applicants are asked to identify the ONE Campaign issues they are most passionate about.

These include:

Foreign Assistance

Advocacy around international assistance and the investments needed to support development and reduce inequality.

Global Health

This includes issues such as:

  • Vaccines
  • Ending malaria
  • Tuberculosis
  • HIV/AIDS
  • Strengthening global health systems

Partnerships Between Canada and Africa

Applicants can express an interest in strengthening relationships and partnerships between Canada and African countries.

Energy Partnerships With Africa

The program also welcomes people interested in creating stronger energy partnerships with Africa.

Sharing African Stories

Participants can also focus on communicating African stories and perspectives and helping ensure that African experiences receive greater visibility in public conversations.

Applicants may also identify another area of interest if it does not fall directly within the listed categories.

Who Should Apply?

The program is intended for people who are passionate about global justice and interested in taking action on issues affecting Africa and international development.

People with experience or training in areas such as the following may find the opportunity particularly relevant:

  • Public speaking
  • Social media
  • Event planning
  • Writing, including blogs and opinion articles
  • Grassroots organizing
  • Political campaigns
  • Legislation and budgets
  • Advocacy
  • Community engagement
  • Communications

However, applicants are not restricted to people with experience in every one of these areas. The application allows individuals to identify the areas where they have relevant training, education or experience and to indicate areas where they would like additional training.

For more information visit HERE.

Leadership Experience

Applicants are also asked about leadership positions they currently hold or have previously held in other organizations.

This gives applicants an opportunity to demonstrate their involvement in organizations, communities, campaigns, volunteer activities or other initiatives where they have taken responsibility or helped lead others.

Commitment Required

The ONE Canada Global Activist program requires participants to dedicate a few hours each month to the program.

There may also be occasional requirements to attend:

  • In-person events
  • Trainings
  • Advocacy activities
  • Other program-related activities

Applicants must therefore be able to commit to participating between October 2026 and October 2027.

Before applying, prospective applicants should consider whether they can realistically maintain this commitment alongside school, employment, volunteering or other responsibilities.

Important Eligibility Requirement

One of the most important conditions for this opportunity is that applicants must be residents of Canada.

The application form specifically requires applicants to confirm that they are residents of Canada.

Therefore, although the program focuses significantly on issues affecting Africa and welcomes people interested in partnerships between Canada and Africa, being based in Canada is a requirement for participation.

People living outside Canada, including applicants currently residing in other African countries, cannot qualify for this particular Canada-based cohort simply because they are interested in African development.

Age Requirement

The ONE Canada Global Activist program is open to all ages, while placing particular focus on youth.

The application asks applicants whether they are 35 years old or younger.

This means the program is not presented as an opportunity exclusively for people under 35, but younger applicants are an important target group.

African Diaspora Participation

Applicants will also be asked whether they are members of the African diaspora.

This question is included as part of the application and allows ONE to understand the backgrounds and communities represented among applicants.

However, the application information does not state that being part of the African diaspora is a requirement for applying. The central geographic eligibility condition is Canadian residency.

Previous ONE Global Activists

Applicants are asked whether they have previously participated as a ONE Global Activist in Canada during either the:

  • 2024–2025 cohort; or
  • 2025–2026 cohort.

This indicates that the application is designed to identify both new applicants and individuals who may have previously participated in the program.

Program Period

Successful participants are expected to commit to the program for approximately one year.

The stated program period is:

October 2026 – October 2027

Applicants should therefore be prepared to participate throughout this period and meet the program’s monthly time commitment.

Application Deadline

The deadline to complete the application is:

August 31, 2026

Applicants should complete the entire application form before the deadline rather than waiting until the final day.

Before submitting, applicants should make sure that all required personal information and application questions have been completed accurately.

Information to Prepare Before Applying

Applicants should be prepared to provide information including:

  • Preferred pronouns
  • First and last name
  • Email address
  • Phone number
  • City
  • Region
  • Postal code
  • Country
  • Current occupation
  • Whether they are part of the African diaspora
  • Whether they are 35 or younger
  • Previous participation in the ONE Global Activists program
  • ONE campaign issues they are passionate about
  • Their motivation for joining the program
  • Areas of training, education or experience
  • Other organizations they are involved with
  • Their ability to commit between October 2026 and October 2027
  • Current or previous leadership roles
  • Areas where they would like additional training

Applicants should think carefully about their motivation and experience before beginning the application because several questions require written responses.

How to Strengthen Your Application

Applicants can improve the quality of their application by clearly connecting their interests and experience to the goals of the program.

1. Explain Your Motivation Clearly

When answering why you want to become a Global Activist, avoid giving a generic response.

Instead, explain what specifically motivates you to work on issues such as global health, Africa-Canada partnerships, foreign assistance, energy partnerships or sharing African stories.

2. Highlight Relevant Experience

Think broadly about your experience.

Relevant experience could include:

  • Volunteering
  • Student leadership
  • Community projects
  • Social media campaigns
  • Writing
  • Public speaking
  • Event organization
  • Advocacy
  • Youth initiatives
  • Nonprofit activities
  • Political or civic engagement

3. Show Your Interest in Advocacy

The program is specifically designed around advocacy, so applicants should demonstrate that they are interested in creating change and engaging people around important issues.

4. Be Specific About Training Needs

The application asks whether there are specific areas where you would like to receive training.

Use this question to identify genuine areas where developing additional skills would help you become a stronger advocate.

5. Demonstrate Your Ability to Commit

Because the program runs from October 2026 to October 2027 and requires a few hours each month, applicants should demonstrate that they understand the commitment and can participate consistently.

Application Process

Interested individuals should first review the official ONE Canada Global Activist information sheet and Frequently Asked Questions before completing the application.

The application is completed online and requires applicants to answer questions about their interests, experience, leadership background, availability and motivation.

Applicants must confirm that they are residents of Canada.

The application must be completed by August 31, 2026.

Privacy and Communications

As part of the application process, applicants are provided with privacy information concerning how their information is handled.

The form also gives applicants the option of signing up for communications from ONE about opportunities to take action on global inequality and related issues.

Applicants can choose whether they want to receive these communications.

The application also notes that submitting the form involves agreement to ONE’s privacy policy, including provisions concerning the transfer of information to ONE.org’s servers in the United States.

Why This Opportunity Matters

The ONE Canada Global Activist program provides an opportunity to move beyond simply learning about global development issues and become involved in advocacy.

For participants, the program can provide a combination of:

  • Advocacy training
  • Political and policy knowledge
  • Communications experience
  • Media skills
  • Networking
  • Community engagement
  • Leadership development
  • Opportunities to interact with elected officials
  • Exposure to international development and development finance
  • Participation in a global activist network

The experience may be particularly valuable for people interested in careers or future opportunities involving international development, nonprofit organizations, communications, public policy, advocacy, government relations and social impact.

Final Thoughts

The ONE Canada Global Activists 2026–2027 program is an opportunity for people in Canada who want to become more active in advocating for global justice, stronger Canada-Africa partnerships and investments that support economic opportunities and healthier lives in Africa.

Participants can gain practical advocacy and communications skills, connect with activists across Canada and internationally, engage with elected officials and receive support for community-based actions.

The program runs from October 2026 to October 2027, requires a commitment of a few hours per month and may include occasional in-person events and training.

Most importantly, prospective applicants should remember that Canadian residency is a mandatory eligibility requirement.

If you are a Canadian resident who is passionate about Africa, global health, international development, advocacy or social justice, and you can commit to participating throughout the 2026–2027 program period, this could be a valuable opportunity to develop your advocacy skills while contributing to campaigns for global change.

Application deadline: August 31, 2026.

Official application: https://act.one.org/survey/global-activist-application-canada-2026/

Opportunity Category

Category: Volunteer / Advocacy Leadership Program (ONE Global Activist program)

Who Qualifies?

Primary eligible group: Individuals who are residents of Canada.

Age: The program is open to all ages, with a particular focus on youth. Applicants are asked whether they are 35 or under.

Background: Applicants can come from different professional, educational and community backgrounds. Experience in public speaking, social media, event planning, writing, grassroots organizing, political campaigns, legislation/budgets or related areas can be relevant.

Geographic eligibility: This specific ONE Canada program requires applicants to be resident in Canada. It is therefore not open to people applying solely from Kenya or other African countries while residing outside Canada.

African diaspora: Applicants are asked whether they are members of the African diaspora, but the application information does not state that African-diaspora status is a requirement.

Commitment: Successful applicants must be able to participate from October 2026 to October 2027, dedicating a few hours per month and potentially attending occasional in-person events and training.

Deadline

August 31, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming economies, governments, industries, scientific research, and everyday life. As increasingly capable AI systems are developed and deployed, there is growing demand for professionals who understand how advanced AI can be governed responsibly while enabling innovation.

Google DeepMind is seeking an experienced Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy to help shape governance frameworks, safety standards, regulatory approaches, government evaluation protocols, and external oversight mechanisms for frontier artificial intelligence systems.

This is a senior-level opportunity for a professional with substantial experience in public policy, national security, AI governance, or the artificial intelligence industry, combined with specific experience in frontier AI safety and governance.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work from either London, United Kingdom, or Washington, D.C., United States, subject to the working-location arrangements associated with the position.

Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy – Google DeepMind

The Governance Manager will operate at the intersection of artificial intelligence, public policy, safety, security, regulation, international standards, and risk management.

Google DeepMind describes AI as one of humanity’s most transformative technologies and emphasizes the importance of developing advanced AI responsibly. The role is therefore designed for an experienced professional capable of helping translate emerging AI governance expectations into practical internal processes while also contributing to external standards and oversight frameworks.

The position involves substantial engagement with governments, international standards organizations, industry coalitions, technical experts, auditors, and other stakeholders involved in the governance of advanced AI.

Opportunity Details

  • Organization: Google DeepMind
  • Position: Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy
  • Opportunity category: Job
  • Career area: AI Governance, Public Policy, AI Safety and Security
  • Work locations: London, United Kingdom; Washington, D.C., United States
  • Level: Experienced/Senior professional
  • Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience
  • Minimum professional experience: 7 years in public policy, national security, or the AI industry
  • Frontier AI experience: At least 3 years focused on frontier AI safety and governance
  • Language: English proficiency is required unless otherwise stated
  • United States compensation: $188,000–$205,000 USD plus a 15% target bonus
  • Deadline: No specific application deadline is provided in the supplied vacancy information. Applicants should therefore check the official vacancy page and apply while the position remains open.

What Is the Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy Role About?

The role focuses on developing and influencing governance systems for increasingly capable AI models.

As frontier AI systems become more powerful, organizations need effective mechanisms for assessing their risks, establishing technical and governance standards, responding to incidents, working with governments, and ensuring that safety practices are integrated into the development and deployment lifecycle.

The Governance Manager will help address these challenges by connecting external developments in AI governance with Google’s internal safety and security functions.

This makes the position particularly relevant to professionals who have worked across areas such as:

  • AI policy and regulation
  • Frontier AI safety
  • Technology governance
  • National security
  • Public policy
  • AI risk management
  • Technical standards
  • Government relations
  • Regulatory affairs
  • AI auditing and assurance
  • Incident disclosure frameworks
  • International governance
  • Responsible AI
  • AI security

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants are expected to meet several core requirements before being considered for the position.

1. Bachelor’s Degree or Equivalent Practical Experience

Candidates must have a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

The vacancy does not restrict applicants to a particular undergraduate discipline. Relevant academic backgrounds may include fields such as public policy, international relations, political science, law, computer science, technology policy, national security, economics, engineering, or other disciplines connected to AI governance and policy.

Equivalent practical experience may also be considered where applicable.

2. At Least Seven Years of Relevant Professional Experience

Candidates need seven years of experience in public policy, national security, or within the AI industry.

This requirement demonstrates that the role is intended for an established professional rather than an entry-level applicant.

Relevant experience could potentially include work involving:

  • Government policy
  • Technology regulation
  • National security policy
  • AI industry strategy
  • AI governance
  • Public-sector technology policy
  • Regulatory affairs
  • International technology standards
  • AI safety policy
  • Government relations
  • Risk and compliance
  • Emerging technology policy

Applicants should clearly demonstrate the connection between their previous work and the responsibilities of a frontier AI governance position.

3. Three Years Focused on Frontier AI Safety and Governance

In addition to the broader seven-year experience requirement, applicants need at least three years of experience specifically focused on frontier AI safety and governance.

This is an important distinction.

General technology experience alone may not be sufficient. Candidates should be able to demonstrate meaningful professional involvement in questions surrounding the safety, governance, oversight, regulation, evaluation, or risk management of highly capable AI systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Google DeepMind also identifies several additional experiences that could strengthen an application.

Experience Connecting AI Safety and Internal Risk Management

Candidates with experience connecting AI safety best practices with internal risk management systems may be particularly well suited to the role.

This could involve developing organizational processes that identify AI-related risks, establishing safeguards, coordinating risk assessments, or integrating safety requirements into product and technology decision-making.

Experience With Third-Party Testing and Auditing

Experience designing, negotiating, or managing third-party testing protocols, incident disclosure frameworks, or auditing regimes is another desirable qualification.

This is significant because external evaluation and independent oversight can play an important role in establishing confidence in advanced AI systems.

Candidates with experience working with external evaluators, auditors, testing organizations, regulators, or government assessment programs may therefore have relevant expertise.

Experience Developing Technical and Governance Standards

The organization is also interested in professionals who have a track record of drafting, negotiating, or influencing technical and governance standards.

Applicants should emphasize occasions where they contributed to:

  • Technical standards
  • Governance frameworks
  • Industry standards
  • Regulatory frameworks
  • Policy guidelines
  • International agreements
  • Risk-management standards
  • AI safety protocols

Where possible, candidates should explain their individual contribution and the outcome of the work rather than simply listing standards-related responsibilities.

High-Trust International AI Safety Network

Another preferred qualification is an established, high-trust network of global AI safety contacts.

The vacancy specifically highlights relationships involving senior government officials, think tanks, and technical policy experts in major AI policy markets, particularly:

  • United States
  • United Kingdom
  • European Union

This suggests that stakeholder engagement and trusted relationships will be an important part of the position.

Key Responsibilities

The Governance Manager will have a broad range of responsibilities involving international standards, government evaluations, incident reporting, internal safety practices, and external oversight.

1. Engage With International Standards Bodies

One of the responsibilities is engaging with international standards organizations such as ISO and INCITS, as well as industry coalitions including the Frontier Model Forum (FMF).

The objective is to contribute to the development of technical benchmarks and best practices for advanced AI.

This means the successful candidate may participate in discussions about how frontier AI systems should be evaluated, governed, tested, and monitored.

The role therefore requires someone who can understand complex technical and policy discussions and translate them into practical governance outcomes.

2. Establish Government Model-Evaluation Protocols

The position involves establishing and overseeing steady-state protocols for unclassified and classified government model evaluations.

Government evaluation of advanced AI systems can involve highly sensitive information and complex institutional requirements.

The Governance Manager will therefore need to understand how evaluation frameworks can be structured and maintained while addressing security, confidentiality, safety, and governance considerations.

3. Develop Cross-Border Incident Disclosure Frameworks

Another major responsibility involves negotiating frameworks for cross-border incident disclosure.

As AI systems operate across jurisdictions, AI-related incidents may have implications for multiple countries and regulatory environments.

The Governance Manager will help establish approaches for determining how relevant incidents are disclosed and coordinated internationally.

This requires strong negotiation skills, knowledge of regulatory environments, and an understanding of how different jurisdictions approach AI safety and security.

4. Connect External Regulation With Internal AI Safety Teams

The successful candidate will act as a bridge between external regulatory developments and internal safety and security teams.

This is one of the central features of the position.

AI regulations, standards, government policies, and industry expectations are continually evolving. The Governance Manager will need to understand these developments and translate them into practical internal processes.

This may involve:

  • Monitoring regulatory developments
  • Interpreting emerging standards
  • Advising internal stakeholders
  • Coordinating with safety teams
  • Supporting compliance planning
  • Translating policy requirements into operational practices
  • Helping inform AI system launch decisions

5. Shape External Oversight Policies

The role also involves helping establish policies for external oversight of advanced AI systems.

This includes defining:

  • Auditor criteria
  • Access protocols
  • External evaluation requirements
  • Oversight mechanisms
  • Positions on regulatory regimes

The successful candidate will therefore contribute to how external organizations and independent experts can assess advanced AI systems.

Why This Google DeepMind Opportunity Is Significant

The Governance Manager position is particularly significant because AI governance is becoming an increasingly important area of technology policy.

Governments and international organizations are developing new approaches to the regulation and oversight of artificial intelligence. At the same time, AI companies are establishing internal safety frameworks and participating in international discussions about standards and responsible development.

A professional in this position can therefore contribute to decisions that influence how frontier AI systems are evaluated and governed.

The role combines several disciplines that are traditionally separate, including:

  1. Artificial intelligence
  2. Public policy
  3. National security
  4. International relations
  5. Technical standards
  6. Risk management
  7. Regulatory affairs
  8. AI safety
  9. Government engagement
  10. Corporate governance

This makes it a particularly specialized career opportunity.

Salary and Compensation

For the United States location, the vacancy lists a compensation range of:

$188,000 to $205,000 USD, plus a 15% target bonus.

The exact compensation offered to an individual may depend on factors including job-related skills, professional experience, education, training, and other relevant considerations.

The supplied vacancy information does not provide a separate salary figure for the London location.

Google also provides employee benefits, with details available through its careers resources.

Applicants should review the official employment terms and benefits information applicable to their selected working location.

Work Locations

Applicants are given the opportunity to indicate their preferred working location between:

London, United Kingdom

London is one of the world’s major centers for technology policy, financial services, international organizations, government relations, and AI research.

The location can be particularly relevant to professionals working across European AI regulation and international technology governance.

Washington, D.C., United States

Washington, D.C. is a major center for government, national security, public policy, technology regulation, and international affairs.

The location may therefore be particularly relevant for professionals whose experience includes U.S. government policy, national security, AI regulation, or technology governance.

Applicants should indicate their preferred location according to the arrangements specified in the vacancy.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is best suited to experienced professionals rather than recent graduates.

Potential applicants may include professionals working in:

  • AI governance
  • AI safety policy
  • Technology policy
  • Public policy
  • National security
  • Government affairs
  • Regulatory affairs
  • AI risk management
  • Responsible AI
  • Technology standards
  • International technology policy
  • AI auditing and assurance
  • Emerging technology governance
  • AI industry policy

Candidates should be able to demonstrate substantial professional experience and, importantly, specialized experience relating to frontier AI safety and governance.

How to Strengthen Your Application

Because this is a highly specialized senior position, applicants should avoid submitting a generic CV.

1. Highlight Frontier AI Experience

Your CV should clearly identify your experience with frontier AI safety and governance.

Do not simply state that you have worked in technology. Explain your specific involvement in AI safety, governance, regulation, evaluation, risk, or standards.

2. Demonstrate Policy Impact

Where possible, quantify or explain the impact of your work.

For example, identify:

  • Policies you helped develop
  • Standards you influenced
  • Regulatory frameworks you contributed to
  • Government stakeholders you engaged
  • AI safety programs you helped establish
  • Auditing or testing frameworks you managed
  • International initiatives you supported

3. Emphasize Cross-Sector Collaboration

The position requires interaction with governments, technical experts, industry groups, standards organizations, auditors, and internal teams.

Your application should therefore demonstrate your ability to work effectively across sectors and disciplines.

4. Showcase Negotiation Skills

Negotiation is particularly relevant to the responsibilities involving incident disclosure frameworks, standards, government evaluations, and external oversight.

Provide concrete evidence of situations in which you successfully negotiated complex policy or governance matters.

5. Demonstrate International Experience

The position has a strong international dimension.

Applicants should highlight experience involving multiple countries, international organizations, multinational stakeholders, or cross-border technology governance where applicable.

6. Explain Technical Policy Expertise Clearly

Applicants do not necessarily need to be AI researchers, but they should be capable of engaging meaningfully with technical AI safety and governance discussions.

Your CV and application materials should demonstrate that you can understand technical issues and translate them into policy and governance decisions.

English Language Requirement

Google states that English proficiency is required for all roles unless otherwise stated in the job posting.

Applicants should therefore be able to communicate effectively in English in professional, policy, technical, and stakeholder-facing environments.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Google states that it is committed to equal employment opportunity and a workforce that represents the users it serves.

The organization’s stated employment policy covers a broad range of protected characteristics and prohibits discrimination on protected grounds under applicable law.

Applicants who require accommodation during the recruitment process can use Google’s designated accommodation process.

Important Recruitment Information

Google also provides several important instructions for candidates and recruitment agencies.

Recruitment Agencies

The company states that it does not accept agency CVs and asks recruitment agencies not to forward unsolicited CVs to Google employees or recruitment addresses.

Applicant Privacy

Information submitted through a Google Careers profile and job application is subject to Google’s applicant and candidate privacy policies.

Applicants should review the relevant privacy information before submitting their personal information.

Deadline

No specific closing date is stated in the job information provided.

Because vacancies can close when hiring requirements are met, interested candidates should not assume that the position will remain available indefinitely.

Applicants should verify the current status of the vacancy on the official Google Careers platform before preparing and submitting their application.

How to Apply

Interested professionals should apply through the official Google Careers recruitment system and carefully review the vacancy requirements before submitting an application.

Applicants should ensure that their CV accurately reflects their professional history, AI governance experience, policy expertise, and relevant achievements.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy position?

It is a senior professional role at Google DeepMind focused on frontier AI governance, safety policy, regulatory developments, technical standards, government evaluations, incident disclosure, and external oversight.

Where is the position based?

The listed working locations are London, United Kingdom, and Washington, D.C., United States. Applicants have the opportunity to share their preferred working location.

What degree is required?

A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience is required.

How much professional experience is required?

Candidates need at least seven years of experience in public policy, national security, or the AI industry, including three years focused on frontier AI safety and governance.

Is AI governance experience important?

Yes. Frontier AI safety and governance experience is specifically identified as a minimum qualification, making it a central requirement rather than simply a preferred skill.

Is the opportunity open to recent graduates?

No. The experience requirements indicate that this is an experienced/senior-level position requiring substantial professional experience.

What is the U.S. salary?

The listed U.S. compensation is $188,000–$205,000 USD plus a 15% target bonus. Individual compensation may vary according to relevant factors.

Is there an application deadline?

No specific deadline is provided in the vacancy information supplied. Candidates should apply as soon as possible while the position remains open.

Can international professionals apply?

The vacancy is associated with London and Washington, D.C., and eligibility will depend on the applicable employment and work-authorization requirements for the selected location. Applicants outside the United States and United Kingdom should carefully review the official vacancy’s location and authorization requirements before applying.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy at Google DeepMind.

Conclusion

The Governance Manager, Frontier AI Safety and Policy position at Google DeepMind represents a highly specialized career opportunity for an experienced professional working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, safety, public policy, national security, regulation, and governance.

The successful candidate will help shape how advanced AI systems are evaluated and governed by engaging with international standards bodies, governments, industry coalitions, technical policy experts, auditors, and internal safety teams.

The position requires a strong professional foundation, including at least seven years of relevant experience and three years specifically focused on frontier AI safety and governance. Candidates with additional experience in AI risk management, third-party testing, auditing, incident disclosure, technical standards, regulatory policy, and international AI safety networks may be particularly competitive.

With working-location options in London or Washington, D.C., and a U.S. compensation range of $188,000–$205,000 plus a 15% target bonus, this opportunity is particularly relevant to established professionals seeking to contribute to the governance of increasingly capable artificial intelligence.

Since no specific application deadline is provided, qualified professionals should review the official Google Careers listing and consider applying promptly while the vacancy remains open.

item.content:encoded:
The Micro-Learning on Environmental, Social and Climate Standards Based on SECAP is a free, self-guided online learning opportunity designed to help professionals and other interested learners understand how environmental, social and climate standards can contribute to sustainable, inclusive and resilient development.

Delivered through WhatsApp, the micro-learning provides a flexible and mobile-friendly way to explore important sustainability concepts, practical tools and frameworks directly from a phone. Participants can learn at their own pace while engaging with short, focused learning content and an AI-supported chat bot

About the Micro-Learning Course

The course focuses on Environmental, Social and Climate Standards (ESC) inspired by SECAP 2021. It addresses the growing need for sustainable practices in investment projects and inclusive development.

Climate change, ecosystem degradation and social inequalities continue to create major challenges for communities, economies and development projects. The course therefore focuses on how stronger environmental and social practices can contribute to projects that are:

  • Environmentally sustainable
  • Socially inclusive
  • More equitable
  • Climate-resilient
  • Sustainable over the long term

The learning experience also emphasizes the importance of partnerships and knowledge exchange across regions to promote better environmental and social outcomes.

A Flexible WhatsApp-Based Learning Experience

Unlike traditional classroom-based training, this micro-learning programme is designed to be accessed directly through WhatsApp.

This makes the course particularly convenient for people who want to learn without committing to fixed classroom schedules.

Participants can:

  • Access the content from their mobile phone.
  • Learn at their own pace.
  • Explore short and engaging learning materials.
  • Receive AI-supported assistance.
  • Participate in thought-provoking conversations.
  • Develop their understanding of sustainability through bite-sized learning.

The course is self-guided, meaning participants can progress through the learning experience according to their own schedule.

Key Features of the Course

1. Pill-Bite Content

The course uses short, focused pieces of content designed to provide useful insights and encourage meaningful conversations around sustainability and development.

2. AI Support

Participants have access to an intelligent chatbot that provides tailored assistance throughout the learning experience.

This AI-supported approach is intended to make the learning process more interactive and accessible.

3. Mobile Learning Through WhatsApp

The entire learning experience is designed to be accessible through WhatsApp, allowing participants to learn whenever and wherever it is convenient for them.

What Will You Learn?

The micro-learning introduces participants to Environmental, Social and Climate Standards (SECAP) and their role in supporting sustainability, equity and resilience in IFAD-supported projects.

The programme covers a wide range of environmental and social issues, including:

  1. Biodiversity conservation
  2. Resource efficiency
  3. Pollution prevention
  4. Cultural heritage
  5. Indigenous peoples’ rights
  6. Labour and working conditions
  7. Community health and safety
  8. Physical and economic resettlement
  9. Financial intermediaries and direct investments
  10. Climate change

Participants will also explore sustainable approaches to agriculture and rural development, helping them understand how environmental and social considerations can be incorporated into development projects.

Course Structure: 10 Learning Pills

The micro-learning is organized into 10 learning pills, each focusing on a specific area of Environmental, Social and Climate Standards.

Pill 1: Introduction to SECAP

Participants begin by developing an understanding of SECAP and the importance of Environmental, Social and Climate Standards in sustainable development.

Pill 2: Biodiversity Conservation

This section focuses on the importance of protecting biodiversity and incorporating biodiversity considerations into development and investment projects.

Pill 3: Resource Efficiency and Pollution Prevention

Participants explore approaches to using resources efficiently while reducing and preventing pollution.

Pill 4: Cultural Heritage

This learning pill addresses the importance of protecting cultural heritage within development projects.

Pill 5: Indigenous Peoples

Participants explore issues surrounding Indigenous peoples and the importance of respecting their rights within development initiatives.

Pill 6: Labour and Working Conditions

This section examines labour and working conditions as an important component of responsible and sustainable development.

Pill 7: Community Health and Safety

Participants learn about considerations related to protecting the health and safety of communities affected by investment and development projects.

Pill 8: Physical and Economic Resettlement

This module introduces issues associated with physical and economic resettlement and their relevance to sustainable project implementation.

Pill 9: Financial Intermediaries and Direct Investments

Participants explore Environmental, Social and Climate considerations related to financial intermediaries and direct investments.

Pill 10: Climate Change

The final learning pill focuses on climate change and its relevance to sustainable development and investment projects.

What Will Participants Be Able to Do?

By completing the micro-learning, participants are expected to develop practical knowledge that can be applied to real-world sustainability and development challenges.

Participants will be able to:

  • Engage in meaningful conversations about sustainability and development.
  • Understand Environmental, Social and Climate Standards in real-world projects.
  • Apply knowledge to projects involving agriculture and rural development.
  • Use tools and frameworks designed to support sustainable initiatives.
  • Strengthen partnerships and knowledge exchange.
  • Make more informed decisions concerning biodiversity, pollution prevention, labour conditions and other environmental and social issues.
  • Use AI-supported guidance during their learning journey.
  • Learn flexibly through WhatsApp.

Who Can Attend the Course?

The course is designed for a broad audience interested in Environmental, Social and Climate Standards and their impact on investment projects.

The target participants specifically include:

  • Project Management Unit staff.
  • Senior government officials responsible for project oversight.
  • National staff from ministries of agriculture, environment and other relevant sectors.
  • Environmental, Social and Climate regulatory bodies.
  • Environmental, Social and Climate consultants.
  • Contractors.
  • Professionals involved in non-sovereign operations.
  • Other individuals interested in learning about Environmental, Social and Climate Standards and their meaningful impact on investment projects.

The course therefore has relevance for professionals working in government, development projects, agriculture, environmental management, project implementation and related fields.

Why Join This Micro-Learning Course?

Free and Accessible

The course is offered free of charge, making it accessible to learners interested in developing their understanding of sustainability and Environmental, Social and Climate Standards.

Learn at Your Own Pace

Because the course is self-guided, participants can work through the content according to their own availability.

Mobile-Friendly

The WhatsApp-based format means learners can access the programme directly from their phones rather than needing to attend a physical training centre.

Practical Knowledge

The course goes beyond general discussions of sustainability by covering specific standards and issues that arise in real-world development and investment projects.

AI-Assisted Learning

Participants can receive support from an AI-powered chatbot as they progress through the learning experience.

Earn Learning Badges

Participants can collect a badge after completing each learning pill. There are 10 badges available in total, corresponding to the 10 learning pills.

How to Join

Participants can begin the free learning experience through WhatsApp.

Start the Micro-Learning via WhatsApp

The provided course information also indicates that participants can access the learning experience by scanning the QR code available on the official course page.

APPLY HERE

Language and Delivery Format

  • Format: Self-guided micro-learning
  • Delivery: WhatsApp
  • Language: English
  • Location: Online/mobile
  • Cost: Free
  • Learning style: Flexible, self-paced learning
  • AI support: Available through an intelligent chatbot

Is There a Deadline?

The information provided for this course does not state an application or enrolment deadline. Learners should therefore consult the official course page for the latest availability and access information.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Micro-Learning on Environmental, Social and Climate Standards Based on SECAP

Conclusion

The Micro-Learning on Environmental, Social and Climate Standards Based on SECAP provides a flexible way for professionals and other interested individuals to develop practical knowledge about sustainability, environmental protection, social inclusion and climate considerations in development projects.

With 10 learning pills, AI support, WhatsApp-based access, self-paced learning and free participation, the course offers a convenient opportunity to strengthen knowledge of Environmental, Social and Climate Standards without requiring traditional classroom attendance.

For people working in project management, government, agriculture, environmental sectors, development programmes or related areas, the course can provide useful knowledge for understanding and applying sustainability principles to real-world investment and rural development projects.

item.content:encoded:
The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), through the Career Path Development for Employment (CPD4E) project, has announced an Ideas Competition for emerging and small nonprofit and community-based organizations in South Africa. The initiative seeks innovative project proposals capable of creating employment and income-generating opportunities for youth, women, and persons with disabilities within South Africa’s Just Energy Transition.

The competition is particularly relevant for organizations working in skills development, employment creation, entrepreneurship, inclusion, renewable energy, green jobs, community development, and economic empowerment.

Successful applicants will receive funding and capacity-building support to implement innovative and scalable solutions in designated Skills Development Zones in Mpumalanga, Northern Cape, and Eastern Cape.

GIZ South Africa Ideas Competition 2026 at a Glance

  • Opportunity: CPD4E Ideas Competition
  • Implementing organization: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ)
  • Project: Career Path Development for Employment (CPD4E)
  • Commissioned by: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
  • Co-funded by: European Union (EU) and Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO)
  • Implemented in partnership with: Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET)
  • Target applicants: Emerging and small NPOs, CBOs, NGOs and similar organizations
  • Geographical focus: South Africa
  • Focus areas: Employment, income generation, skills development and the Just Energy Transition
  • Priority beneficiaries: Youth, women and persons with disabilities
  • Target areas: Mpumalanga, Northern Cape and Eastern Cape
  • Support: Funding and capacity-building
  • Application deadline: 11 September 2026 at 5:00 PM SAST

What Is the GIZ CPD4E Ideas Competition?

The CPD4E Ideas Competition is designed to identify and support organizations with practical and innovative ideas for addressing employment and income-generation challenges associated with South Africa’s transition toward a more sustainable and inclusive energy economy.

South Africa’s Just Energy Transition involves significant changes to the country’s energy and economic systems. While the transition toward cleaner energy can create new employment opportunities, it can also create challenges for communities and groups that need additional skills, resources, access to employment, and opportunities to participate in emerging industries.

The competition therefore aims to identify solutions that can help people access economic opportunities connected to the transition.

Applicants are encouraged to put forward ideas that are not only innovative but also capable of being implemented, expanded, and replicated in communities.

What Is the Career Path Development for Employment Project?

The Ideas Competition forms part of the Career Path Development for Employment (CPD4E) project.

The project is commissioned by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-funded by the European Union and the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), and implemented by GIZ in partnership with South Africa’s Department of Higher Education and Training.

The broader project is concerned with strengthening pathways toward employment and improving access to skills and economic opportunities.

Through the Ideas Competition, the project seeks to work with organizations that understand local challenges and can develop solutions that respond directly to the needs of communities.

What Is the Main Objective of the Competition?

The central objective is to support innovative and scalable solutions that create employment and income opportunities within South Africa’s Just Energy Transition.

Projects should demonstrate how an organization’s idea can contribute to practical economic opportunities for people who may otherwise experience barriers to employment and participation in emerging sectors.

The competition places particular emphasis on:

  1. Employment creation
  2. Income generation
  3. Skills development
  4. Economic inclusion
  5. Youth opportunities
  6. Women’s economic participation
  7. Inclusion of persons with disabilities
  8. The Just Energy Transition
  9. Innovative approaches
  10. Scalable and sustainable solutions

Who Are the Priority Beneficiaries?

A major feature of the competition is its focus on groups that can face significant barriers when accessing employment and economic opportunities.

Youth

Projects may seek to help young people develop skills, access employment, establish businesses, participate in entrepreneurship, or enter emerging industries associated with the energy transition.

Organizations with practical approaches to youth employment and skills development may therefore find this competition particularly relevant.

Women

The initiative also seeks to support solutions that improve employment and income opportunities for women.

Potential projects could address barriers to women’s participation in economic activities, entrepreneurship, skills development, or emerging opportunities linked to the Just Energy Transition.

Persons With Disabilities

Persons with disabilities are another priority group.

Applicants may develop solutions that improve accessibility, skills development, employment pathways, entrepreneurship opportunities, or participation in economic activities for people with disabilities.

Which Areas of South Africa Are Covered?

The competition specifically identifies three Skills Development Zones:

  • Mpumalanga
  • Northern Cape
  • Eastern Cape

Applicants should therefore pay close attention to the geographical focus of the competition when developing their proposals.

Projects intended for implementation within these areas should demonstrate an understanding of the local context and explain how the proposed intervention can contribute to employment and income opportunities.

What Kind of Ideas Is GIZ Looking For?

The competition is aimed at organizations with innovative ideas that can create jobs within South Africa’s Just Energy Transition.

The announcement does not limit applicants to one specific project model. This creates room for organizations to propose solutions that respond to particular local employment, skills, entrepreneurship, or economic-development challenges.

Potential areas of relevance may include:

  • Skills development linked to emerging green industries
  • Employment pathways for young people
  • Entrepreneurship and income-generation initiatives
  • Women-focused economic empowerment
  • Disability-inclusive employment models
  • Community-based economic development
  • Green skills and workforce preparation
  • Career development initiatives
  • Job matching and employment support
  • Innovative approaches to vocational skills
  • Small-business development
  • Local economic opportunities connected to the energy transition
  • Models that can be expanded or replicated in other communities

Applicants should ensure that their actual proposal aligns with the official competition requirements rather than assuming that every project within these broad areas will automatically qualify.

What Support Will Successful Applicants Receive?

Successful applicants will receive two important forms of support.

1. Funding

Selected organizations will receive funding to implement their proposed solutions.

This funding is intended to help successful applicants move their ideas beyond the proposal stage and into practical implementation.

Organizations should therefore demonstrate that their proposed activities are realistic and that the requested support can contribute meaningfully to achieving measurable results.

2. Capacity-Building Support

In addition to financial support, successful applicants will receive capacity-building support.

This is significant for emerging and small organizations because funding alone does not always guarantee successful project implementation.

Capacity-building can help organizations strengthen their ability to plan, manage, implement, monitor, and potentially scale their interventions.

Applicants should therefore consider how their organization can use both financial and non-financial support to strengthen the sustainability of their project.

Why Is This Opportunity Important?

The GIZ Ideas Competition provides an opportunity for smaller and emerging organizations to contribute to one of South Africa’s major economic and development transitions.

For communities affected by changes in the energy sector, the Just Energy Transition is not only an environmental issue. It also involves questions about jobs, skills, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, inclusion, and economic resilience.

Organizations working directly with communities can often identify challenges that larger institutions may not see. Supporting these organizations can therefore help develop solutions that are grounded in local realities.

The competition’s focus on youth, women, and persons with disabilities also highlights the importance of ensuring that the benefits of economic transformation reach groups that may face barriers to participation.

Why Should Organizations Apply?

There are several potential advantages for eligible organizations.

Financial Support

Successful applicants will receive funding to implement their selected project ideas.

Capacity Development

Organizations will receive capacity-building support that can strengthen their institutional and project implementation capabilities.

Opportunity to Test an Innovative Idea

The competition provides organizations with an opportunity to turn an innovative concept into a practical intervention.

Contribution to the Just Energy Transition

Successful projects can contribute directly to creating employment and income opportunities within South Africa’s transition toward a more sustainable energy economy.

Focus on Underserved Groups

Organizations can develop solutions that specifically address employment and economic opportunities for youth, women, and persons with disabilities.

Potential for Scalability

The competition specifically emphasizes innovative and scalable solutions, meaning applicants should think beyond a one-time activity and consider how their approach could potentially reach more people or be replicated elsewhere.

What Makes a Strong Project Proposal?

Organizations preparing an application should avoid presenting only a general idea. A strong proposal should clearly explain the problem, the proposed solution, the target beneficiaries, the implementation approach, and the expected results.

Applicants should consider demonstrating:

A Clearly Defined Problem

Explain the employment, skills, income, or economic challenge that the project intends to address.

An Innovative Solution

Describe what makes the proposed approach different, practical, or more effective than existing approaches.

Clear Beneficiaries

Identify who will benefit from the project and explain how youth, women, and/or persons with disabilities will be reached.

Local Relevance

Explain the connection between the project and the relevant Skills Development Zone.

Employment and Income Potential

Clearly demonstrate how the project could contribute to employment creation, income generation, entrepreneurship, or improved access to economic opportunities.

Feasibility

Show that the organization has a realistic plan for implementing the proposed activities.

Scalability

Explain how the solution could potentially expand, reach additional beneficiaries, or be replicated in other locations.

Sustainability

Consider what will happen after the initial project support ends and how the intervention could continue producing benefits.

How to Prepare Before Applying

Organizations interested in participating should begin preparations well before the deadline.

A useful preparation process can include:

  1. Review the official competition information carefully.
  2. Confirm that the organization meets the applicant requirements.
  3. Identify the specific employment or income challenge being addressed.
  4. Define the target beneficiaries.
  5. Develop a clear and innovative solution.
  6. Establish how the project connects to the Just Energy Transition.
  7. Determine how the project will operate in the relevant geographical area.
  8. Develop measurable objectives and expected results.
  9. Prepare a realistic implementation approach.
  10. Consider scalability and long-term sustainability.
  11. Gather the organizational information and supporting documents required by the official application process.
  12. Submit the proposal before the stated deadline.

Important Deadline

The closing date for the GIZ South Africa CPD4E Ideas Competition is:

11 September 2026 at 5:00 PM SAST.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their proposals. Organizations should allow sufficient time to review the requirements, develop their project concept, prepare supporting information, and complete the submission process.

Who Can Apply?

The competition is targeted at emerging and small NPOs, CBOs, NGOs and similar organizations.

The opportunity is therefore designed for organizations rather than individual applicants seeking personal scholarships, internships, or employment.

Eligible organizations should carefully review the official call for proposals to confirm the precise organizational eligibility criteria and any additional requirements before submitting an application.

Countries and Continents Eligible to Apply

This is a South Africa-focused opportunity. The announcement specifically refers to project implementation within Skills Development Zones in Mpumalanga, Northern Cape, and Eastern Cape.

Therefore, organizations should not interpret the competition as a general worldwide funding opportunity. Organizations seeking to apply should verify the official call for proposals for the precise geographical and organizational eligibility requirements.

The primary geographical focus is South Africa, Africa.

APPLY HERE

Who Is the Opportunity Best Suited For?

The competition may be particularly suitable for small or emerging organizations working in areas such as:

  • Youth employment
  • Women’s economic empowerment
  • Disability inclusion
  • Skills development
  • Vocational training
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Community development
  • Employment services
  • Green jobs
  • Renewable energy-related skills
  • Economic empowerment
  • Social innovation
  • Just Energy Transition initiatives
  • Income-generation programmes

Organizations should, however, ensure that their proposed activities meet the specific requirements contained in the official call for proposals.

Pro Tip for Applicants

A strong application should do more than describe a good idea. It should demonstrate a clear connection between the problem, solution, beneficiaries, implementation plan, employment outcomes, and Just Energy Transition.

Applicants should make it easy for reviewers to understand:

What is the problem? → Who is affected? → What is the proposed solution? → How will it create jobs or income? → Why is the solution innovative? → How will it be implemented? → How can it be scaled?

A proposal that clearly answers these questions can communicate its potential impact much more effectively.

Visit HERE to learn more about the GIZ South Africa Ideas Competition 2026

About the Organizations Behind the Competition

The CPD4E project is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and co-funded by the European Union (EU) and the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO).

Implementation is led by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) in partnership with South Africa’s Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET).

The partnership brings together international development cooperation and South African institutional expertise to support employment and skills-related outcomes.

Final Thoughts

The GIZ South Africa CPD4E Ideas Competition represents an important opportunity for emerging and small nonprofit, community-based, and similar organizations with innovative ideas for creating employment and income opportunities within South Africa’s Just Energy Transition.

With funding and capacity-building support available to successful applicants, the competition can help organizations move promising ideas toward practical implementation. Its focus on youth, women, and persons with disabilities also makes inclusion a central component of the opportunity.

Organizations operating in or connected to the targeted Skills Development Zones in Mpumalanga, Northern Cape, and Eastern Cape should carefully review the official call for proposals and develop applications that demonstrate innovation, feasibility, measurable employment or income outcomes, and potential for scalability.

The application deadline is 11 September 2026 at 5:00 PM SAST, so interested organizations should begin preparing their proposals early and ensure that all submission requirements are satisfied before the closing time.

item.content:encoded:
CorpsAfrica is seeking an experienced and strategic African Philanthropy Director to lead philanthropic revenue generation and fundraising capacity-building across its growing African network.

This is a senior leadership opportunity for an experienced nonprofit fundraising professional who understands African markets and has a strong track record in major donor cultivation, institutional grants, philanthropic strategy and revenue generation.

The position is Africa-based, with remote or hybrid flexibility within countries where CorpsAfrica operates.

About CorpsAfrica

Founded in 2011 by former Peace Corps Volunteer Liz Fanning, CorpsAfrica was created in response to a need for Africans to have opportunities to serve and support communities within their own countries.

The organisation recruits and trains young Africans to live and serve in rural communities. Volunteers work directly with local communities, listening to residents and facilitating community-led development projects.

Since launching its first Volunteer cohort in Morocco in 2013, CorpsAfrica has expanded to 11 African countries.

According to the opportunity information, more than 1,700 Volunteers have completed their service, working with communities to implement small-scale, high-impact projects identified by local people. These efforts have contributed to improving the lives of nearly one million people across the continent.

About the African Philanthropy Director Position

The African Philanthropy Director is a senior position within CorpsAfrica’s Global Support Office (GSO).

The primary purpose of the role is to strengthen CorpsAfrica’s ability to generate philanthropic revenue across Africa and build the fundraising capacity of its country offices.

The Director will focus specifically on:

  • Strategic revenue generation
  • Donor acquisition
  • Major donor cultivation
  • Institutional fundraising
  • Pipeline expansion
  • Local philanthropic giving
  • Fundraising capacity building
  • Revenue analytics
  • Donor relationship management

The successful candidate will also serve as a strategic leader and executive coach for country-level Philanthropy Officers.

Rather than focusing primarily on general partnerships or programme management, the position is specifically designed around unlocking fundraising potential through African individual donors, major gifts, institutional funding and other philanthropic channels.

Key Responsibilities

1. Strategic Coaching and Institutional Capacity Building

A major part of the position involves helping CorpsAfrica’s country teams strengthen their fundraising capabilities.

The African Philanthropy Director will:

  • Serve as a strategic fundraising coach and adviser to Country Directors.
  • Work with country office Boards of Directors and Local Councils.
  • Support Philanthropy Officers across the network.
  • Develop strategies for increasing local revenue generation.
  • Create and deliver fundraising training programmes.
  • Develop localized training modules covering major donor cultivation, pitch development, grant writing, local philanthropy and high-value fundraising.
  • Conduct one-on-one coaching sessions with local teams.
  • Review fundraising pipelines and identify areas for improvement.
  • Troubleshoot fundraising pitches and strategies.
  • Help country teams optimize their local revenue plans.
  • Develop standardized fundraising toolkits.
  • Create customized proposal templates.
  • Develop donor pitch decks and grant application guidelines for country offices.

The goal is to ensure that fundraising capacity becomes stronger within individual country offices rather than remaining concentrated at the global level.

2. Donor Cultivation and Global Pipeline Leadership

The Director will also play an important role in building and maintaining relationships with potential and existing funders.

Responsibilities include:

  • Designing donor stewardship frameworks.
  • Supporting long-term donor engagement and retention.
  • Cultivating relationships with high-net-worth individuals.
  • Working with foundations and institutional funders.
  • Supporting country offices in identifying potential major donors.
  • Researching philanthropic organisations and funding opportunities.
  • Helping country teams develop high-potential fundraising prospects.
  • Overseeing the organisational grant calendar.
  • Leading the development of high-value proposals.
  • Writing and editing concept notes.
  • Supporting major institutional grant applications.

The successful candidate will therefore need strong relationship-building, writing, strategic fundraising and donor management skills.

3. Revenue Analytics, CRM Governance and Reporting

The position also has a strong data and financial management component.

The African Philanthropy Director will be responsible for helping the organisation track and understand its fundraising performance.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Building and maintaining network-wide fundraising dashboards.
  • Tracking donor retention.
  • Monitoring average gift sizes.
  • Analysing conversion rates.
  • Developing multi-year revenue projections.
  • Maintaining accurate fundraising pipeline information.
  • Supporting CRM governance across country offices.
  • Ensuring donor pipeline data is accurate.
  • Monitoring grant schedules.
  • Supporting accurate financial gift processing.
  • Preparing fundraising analytics for senior leadership.
  • Developing revenue forecasts.
  • Preparing strategic fundraising reports for the CEO and Board of Directors.

Experience with enterprise CRM platforms such as Salesforce is therefore particularly important for this position.

Qualifications and Experience

CorpsAfrica is looking for an experienced fundraising and nonprofit leader with substantial experience in philanthropic revenue generation.

Education

Applicants should have:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Non-Profit Management, Business Administration, International Development, Executive Leadership or a related field.

A Master’s degree is preferred, although equivalent executive-level experience may also be considered.

Professional Experience

Applicants should have at least:

  • 7+ years of progressive leadership experience in nonprofit fundraising, major donor cultivation, institutional grant securing or philanthropic strategy.
  • Demonstrated experience working across African markets.
  • A proven record of securing major gifts.
  • Experience securing institutional grants.
  • Experience obtaining multi-year funding commitments.

Coaching and Leadership

The role requires substantial experience in:

  • Training teams.
  • Coaching professionals.
  • Mentoring fundraising staff.
  • Working across different cultural environments.
  • Supporting international or geographically diverse teams.
  • Building fundraising capacity within organisations.

Technical Skills

Candidates should have strong technical capabilities, particularly in:

  • Enterprise CRM systems such as Salesforce.
  • Donor pipeline tracking.
  • Fundraising analytics.
  • Revenue reporting.
  • Financial forecasting.
  • Performance dashboards.

Financial Skills

The successful candidate should demonstrate strong financial understanding, including:

  • Budget management.
  • Revenue forecasting.
  • Fundraising target tracking.
  • Financial performance analysis.

Communication Skills

Excellent communication skills are essential.

Candidates should have strong abilities in:

  • Written communication.
  • Oral communication.
  • Donor presentations.
  • Fundraising pitches.
  • Proposal writing.
  • Editing concept notes.
  • Developing institutional funding applications.

Commitment to CorpsAfrica’s Mission

CorpsAfrica is looking for someone who has a genuine commitment to:

  • Youth leadership.
  • Community-led development.
  • African philanthropy.
  • Strengthening local fundraising capacity.
  • Expanding opportunities for young Africans to serve their communities.

Location and Work Arrangement

The position is described as Africa-based, with remote or hybrid flexibility within countries where CorpsAfrica has a presence.

The role is:

  • Full-time
  • Exempt
  • Africa-based
  • Within the Global Support Office structure

The opportunity therefore offers flexibility for an experienced professional based within the organisation’s operational footprint.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply is:

21 August 2026

Interested candidates are encouraged to submit their applications before the stated deadline.

How to Apply

Applicants should submit:

  1. A cover letter explaining their qualifications and experience relevant to the African Philanthropy Director position.
  2. A résumé detailing their professional background, leadership experience and fundraising achievements.

Applications should be submitted through JazzHR.

Only complete applications will be considered.

Equal Opportunity Statement

CorpsAfrica states that it is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from individuals regardless of:

  • Age
  • Gender
  • Race
  • Ethnicity
  • Sexual orientation
  • Marital status
  • Physical ability
  • Other legally protected characteristics

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity is particularly suited to experienced professionals who have already established themselves in nonprofit fundraising, philanthropy or institutional development.

It may be a strong fit for professionals with backgrounds in:

  • Nonprofit fundraising
  • Philanthropic strategy
  • Major donor development
  • Institutional grants
  • International development
  • African philanthropy
  • Fundraising leadership
  • Donor relations
  • Revenue strategy
  • Nonprofit executive leadership

The seniority of the position means it is not an entry-level opportunity. The organisation specifically requires a minimum of seven years of progressive leadership experience in relevant areas.

APPLY HERE

Eligible Applicants

The position is designed for experienced professionals, particularly those with:

  • A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent executive experience.
  • At least seven years of progressive leadership experience in relevant fundraising or philanthropic roles.
  • Experience securing major gifts and institutional grants.
  • Experience working across African markets.
  • Strong fundraising, communication and financial skills.
  • Experience coaching and mentoring teams.
  • Strong CRM and fundraising analytics capabilities.
  • A demonstrated commitment to youth leadership and community-led development.

Conclusion
