item.content:encoded:
The European Committee of the Regions (CoR) offers several opportunities for students, graduates, young professionals and public-sector officials who want to gain practical experience within a European Union institution and understand how local and regional authorities contribute to EU policymaking.

Based in Brussels, Belgium, the CoR provides opportunities through its Cicero traineeship programme, study visits, and study visits for government officials. These programmes allow participants to experience the work of a multilingual and multinational EU institution, engage with European policy issues and develop professional skills in an international environment.

The flagship Cicero traineeship is particularly attractive to university graduates and students who want to gain practical experience in EU affairs. It lasts five months, is full-time, takes place in Brussels and provides a grant of approximately €1,538 per month, together with a travel and mobility allowance.

The application windows depend on the session. For the Spring Session, applications are submitted from 1 July to 1 October at 12:00 noon Brussels time of the preceding year. For the Autumn Session, applications are submitted from 6 January to 31 March at 12:00 noon Brussels time of the same year.

European Committee of the Regions Traineeships: Quick Overview

  • Host institution: European Committee of the Regions
  • Location: Brussels, Belgium
  • Main opportunity: Cicero traineeship
  • Duration: Five months
  • Working arrangement: Full-time, 40 hours per week
  • Financial support: Approximately €1,538 per month
  • Additional support: Travel and mobility allowance
  • Health insurance: Optional
  • Accident insurance: Included
  • Languages: One EU language plus satisfactory English or French
  • Main applicants: University graduates and students meeting the academic requirements
  • EU citizenship: EU citizens are eligible; third-country nationals may be selected in exceptional circumstances
  • Spring session: 16 February to 15 July
  • Spring application period: 1 July to 1 October at 12:00 noon Brussels time of the previous year
  • Autumn session: 16 September to 15 February
  • Autumn application period: 6 January to 31 March at 12:00 noon Brussels time
  • Application: Online

What Is the European Committee of the Regions?

The European Committee of the Regions (CoR) is an EU consultative body representing local and regional authorities across the European Union.

Its work focuses on ensuring that the perspectives of cities, regions and local communities are taken into account in the European decision-making process.

The institution provides a bridge between the EU level and local and regional realities. Its work covers a broad range of policy areas, including areas such as:

  • Regional development
  • Cohesion policy
  • Climate change
  • Employment
  • Education
  • Public procurement
  • Citizenship
  • Security
  • Digital transformation
  • Sustainable development
  • Local governance
  • Economic and social development

For young professionals and graduates interested in European affairs, the CoR offers an opportunity to understand how EU policies interact with the realities of cities and regions.

The institution describes its traineeships as an opportunity to experience a dynamic and relatively human-sized EU institutional environment.

European Committee of the Regions Cicero Traineeship

The Cicero traineeship is the main traineeship opportunity offered by the European Committee of the Regions.

It provides participants with practical experience inside an EU institution while exposing them to a wide range of European policy issues.

A trainee works alongside CoR staff and has the opportunity to observe how the institution operates in a multilingual and multinational environment.

The programme also encourages trainees to be creative and develop projects addressing issues relevant to European regions and cities.

Cicero Traineeship Duration and Working Conditions

The Cicero traineeship lasts five months.

Trainees work:

  • Full-time
  • 40 hours per week
  • At the European Committee of the Regions in Brussels, Belgium

The traineeship is therefore designed as an intensive professional experience rather than a short observational placement.

Participants become part of the institution’s working environment and can gain practical exposure to EU policies, administration, communication, research and other areas depending on their selected department.

Financial Benefits of the Cicero Traineeship

One of the major attractions of the Cicero programme is its financial support.

Selected trainees receive a grant of approximately:

€1,538 per month

In addition to the monthly grant, the programme provides:

  • Travel allowance
  • Mobility allowance
  • Accident insurance
  • Optional health insurance coverage

The financial support can help participants manage some of the costs associated with undertaking a five-month professional experience in Brussels.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the applicable traineeship rules and financial conditions before making arrangements based on the grant amount.

YFactor: Creating Your Own Project at the CoR

A distinctive feature of the Cicero traineeship is the YFactor scheme.

Through this initiative, trainees are encouraged to work on projects addressing issues that are relevant to European regions and cities.

This gives trainees an opportunity to apply creativity and initiative rather than simply performing routine administrative duties.

Depending on their interests and the nature of their project, trainees may develop initiatives such as:

  • Conferences
  • Podcasts
  • E-books
  • Communication projects
  • Policy-related initiatives
  • Other creative projects relevant to the work of the CoR

The experience can therefore provide participants with opportunities to demonstrate project management, communication, research, teamwork and leadership skills.

What Makes the Cicero Traineeship Valuable?

The programme provides more than a line on a CV.

A trainee can gain first-hand exposure to:

  • EU policymaking
  • European institutions
  • Regional and local governance
  • Public administration
  • European cooperation
  • Policy research
  • Institutional communication
  • Multilingual working environments
  • International teamwork
  • Project development

Participants also work alongside colleagues and other trainees from different backgrounds, creating opportunities for professional networking and intercultural learning.

Cicero Traineeship Sessions and Application Deadlines

The CoR runs two main Cicero traineeship sessions each year.

Spring Session

The Spring Session runs from:

16 February to 15 July

The application period is:

1 July to 1 October at 12:00 noon Brussels time of the previous year.

The general selection calendar is:

  • Application period: 1 July–1 October
  • Pre-selection and interviews: November
  • Selection: December
  • Traineeship: 16 February–15 July

For example, applicants seeking a Spring traineeship beginning in February 2027 would apply during the corresponding application period in 2026.

Autumn Session

The Autumn Session runs from:

16 September to 15 February

The application period is:

6 January to 31 March at 12:00 noon Brussels time of the same year.

The general selection calendar is:

  • Application period: 6 January–31 March
  • Pre-selection and interviews: May
  • Selection: June
  • Traineeship: 16 September–15 February

Applicants should always verify the applicable dates for their desired traineeship period before submitting an application.

Important Deadline Warning

The CoR strongly recommends that applicants avoid waiting until the final hours to apply.

High data traffic close to the deadline may affect the successful transmission of an application. Applications that are submitted late or are not successfully received electronically cannot be accepted.

Applicants should therefore submit their forms well before the stated deadline.

Who Can Apply for the Cicero Traineeship?

The Cicero programme is primarily designed for people with a university-level academic background who want to gain professional experience in an EU institutional environment.

Applicants should meet the following requirements.

1. Academic Requirement

Candidates must either:

  • Have obtained a full undergraduate academic degree; or
  • Have completed at least the third year of higher education, at university or an equivalent institution, by the application deadline.

This means that the programme can be relevant to both graduates and students who have already completed the required stage of higher education.

2. Language Requirement

Applicants must be fluent in at least one EU language.

They must also have satisfactory knowledge of:

  • English; or
  • French.

Because the European Committee of the Regions operates in a multilingual institutional environment, language skills are important for successful participation.

3. Nationality

EU citizens can apply.

Citizens of third countries, including the United Kingdom, may also apply and can be selected in exceptional cases.

Third-country applicants must, however, meet the relevant requirements under Belgian national immigration law concerning legal residence and employment in Belgium.

Therefore, non-EU nationality does not automatically make an applicant ineligible, but selection is exceptional and subject to applicable immigration requirements.

Who Is Not Eligible for the Cicero Traineeship?

Certain applicants are specifically excluded from the programme.

You cannot be accepted if you have:

  • Already received more than eight weeks of in-house placement, whether paid or unpaid, in a European institution, body, delegation or representative office; or
  • Had any form of employment in a European institution or body.

Applicants should carefully consider previous placements and employment before applying.

Providing inaccurate information about previous experience can result in rejection or cancellation.

How to Apply for the Cicero Traineeship

Applications are submitted online.

Applicants should follow these steps:

Step 1: Select the Appropriate Traineeship Period

Determine whether you are applying for:

  • The Spring Session; or
  • The Autumn Session.

Make sure you understand the corresponding application window.

Step 2: Choose Your Preferred CoR Departments

Applicants can select up to three preferred CoR departments.

Candidates should research the available departments and choose options that align with their academic background, professional interests and career goals.

Step 3: Complete the Online Application

Applicants must complete all mandatory fields in the online application form.

Information should be entered carefully and accurately.

Step 4: Review Your Application

Before submitting, check:

  • Personal details
  • Academic information
  • Language skills
  • Professional experience
  • Previous EU placements
  • Preferred departments
  • Other required information

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

Only applications submitted electronically and received before the deadline can be considered.

Applicants are permitted to make changes to their application before the deadline.

However, applicants may submit only one application per traineeship period.

Important Rules for Applicants

The CoR emphasizes accuracy and honesty throughout the application process.

Applicants should not exaggerate or provide false information.

False statements can result in:

  • Rejection of the application; or
  • Cancellation of the traineeship after selection.

Applicants should therefore ensure that all academic, professional and personal information is accurate.

Study Visits at the European Committee of the Regions

The CoR also offers study visits for students and other eligible applicants who want to learn more about the role of local and regional authorities in EU policymaking.

Study visits can be particularly useful for students who are:

  • Completing academic research
  • Finalising a university project
  • Working on a thesis
  • Studying European policies
  • Interested in local and regional government
  • Researching areas such as climate change, citizenship, cohesion, public procurement or security

The programme provides an opportunity to complement academic learning with first-hand exposure to an EU consultative institution.

Duration of CoR Study Visits

Study visits normally last:

1 to 4 months

They may be extended to a maximum of:

6 months

depending on available resources.

The starting date is agreed upon with the candidate.

Participants work:

  • Full-time
  • 40 hours per week
  • In Brussels, Belgium

Unlike the Cicero traineeship, the study visit does not provide the same paid grant structure.

Financial and Insurance Arrangements for Study Visits

Study visits are not presented as paid traineeships.

Applicants must provide evidence that they have financial support from another source or that the study visit forms an integral part of their education.

Possible sources of financial support include:

  • University funding
  • Scholarship
  • Grant
  • Public institution
  • Private institution
  • Non-governmental organisation

The CoR does not provide health insurance for study visits.

However:

  • Accident insurance is included.
  • Participants must provide proof of obligatory health insurance covering the entire study visit.

Who Can Apply for a Study Visit?

Applicants should generally meet the following conditions:

  • Be an EU citizen, although third-country nationals may be selected exceptionally
  • Hold at least a Bachelor’s degree; or
  • Have completed at least half of a relevant Bachelor’s degree programme
  • Be fluent in one EU language
  • Have satisfactory knowledge of English or French

Third-country nationals must also comply with the applicable Belgian immigration and residence requirements if selected.

Documents Required for Study Visits

Applicants may be required to provide:

  1. A legible copy of their passport or identity card.
  2. Proof of obligatory health insurance covering the entire study visit.
  3. A copy of their Bachelor’s diploma; or
  4. A certificate confirming that they have successfully completed at least half of a relevant Bachelor’s training cycle.
  5. Documents verifying professional experience listed in the application.

Applicants should prepare these documents in advance to avoid delays.

Study Visits for Government Officials

The European Committee of the Regions also offers a separate study visit scheme for government officials.

This programme is designed for staff members or trainees working for:

  • National public authorities
  • Regional public authorities
  • Local public authorities

within an EU Member State.

The purpose is to strengthen cooperation and networking between the CoR and the participant’s employing institution.

Participants can gain insight into the work of the Committee of the Regions while developing their professional knowledge, skills and competencies.

Duration of Government Official Study Visits

Government official study visits generally last:

2 to 6 months

The Director responsible for Human Resources may authorize an extension, allowing the total period to reach up to:

12 months

The precise starting date is agreed with the participant.

The work is:

  • Full-time
  • 40 hours per week
  • Based in Brussels, Belgium

Are Government Official Study Visits Paid?

No.

Government official study visits are unpaid.

All expenses must be covered by:

  • The participant; or
  • The participant’s sending authority.

The CoR does provide accident insurance.

Applicants should therefore secure appropriate financial arrangements before undertaking the visit.

Who Can Apply for Government Official Study Visits?

Applicants must generally be:

  • Staff members or trainees of a national, regional or local public authority in an EU Member State
  • Qualified at Bachelor’s level or have completed at least half of a relevant Bachelor’s programme
  • Working in a position whose level and responsibilities correspond to duties performed by EU staff within the CoR
  • Highly proficient in English or French

Third-country citizens, including UK citizens, may be selected in exceptional circumstances, subject to the relevant Belgian immigration and residence requirements.

Documents Required for Government Officials

Applicants may be asked to provide:

  • Confirmation of employment from the sending authority
  • Confirmation that the sending authority agrees to the study visit
  • Proof of obligatory health insurance
  • Relevant academic diplomas or official certificates
  • Documents proving professional experience listed in the application

The support of the applicant’s employing authority is therefore an essential component of this particular scheme.

Choosing Between the Three CoR Opportunities

The three schemes serve different purposes.

Opportunity Main Target Group Duration Paid? Location
Cicero Traineeship Graduates and eligible university students 5 months Yes, approx. €1,538/month + allowances Brussels
Study Visit Students and eligible researchers 1–4 months, extendable to 6 No CoR grant; external funding required Brussels
Government Official Study Visit Public authority staff/trainees 2–6 months, potentially up to 12 Unpaid Brussels

This distinction is important because applicants should select the programme that corresponds to their academic and professional circumstances.

Key Benefits of the European Committee of the Regions Opportunities

1. Experience Within an EU Institution

Participants gain first-hand exposure to the functioning of an EU consultative body.

2. Professional Development

The programmes can strengthen:

  • Research skills
  • Communication skills
  • Policy analysis
  • Project management
  • Teamwork
  • Intercultural communication
  • Institutional knowledge

3. International Networking

Brussels is home to numerous European institutions, international organizations, NGOs, think tanks and policy networks.

Working at the CoR provides participants with an opportunity to build professional relationships within an international environment.

4. Exposure to EU Policies

Participants can gain practical insight into policy areas affecting European cities and regions.

5. Multicultural Environment

The CoR operates in a multilingual and multinational environment, allowing participants to work with people from different European and international backgrounds.

6. Opportunity to Develop Independent Projects

Through the YFactor scheme, Cicero trainees can develop creative projects related to European regions and cities.

7. Financial Support for Cicero Trainees

The Cicero traineeship provides a monthly grant and travel and mobility support, making it considerably more financially attractive than the unpaid study visit schemes.

Support for Candidates With Special Needs

The European Committee of the Regions states that it is committed to equal opportunities and a diverse, inclusive and equitable working environment.

Candidates and trainees with:

  • Disabilities
  • Special needs
  • Medical conditions

can request appropriate adjustments to enable them to participate in the selection process and traineeship on an equal basis.

Applicants requiring specific adjustments for:

  • Interviews
  • Selection procedures
  • The traineeship itself

can contact the CoR social worker at:

Social-Service-CoR@cor.europa.eu

Requests are assessed individually, taking into account applicable rules and available resources.

Information provided concerning special needs is treated confidentially and in accordance with applicable data protection requirements.

What Previous Trainees Say About the Experience

The CoR’s testimonials illustrate the range of experiences available to participants.

Previous trainees have highlighted:

  • Building professional and social connections
  • Developing independent projects
  • Learning how public institutions operate
  • Gaining first-hand experience of EU policymaking
  • Personal and professional growth
  • Working in a diverse international environment
  • Understanding the role of young people in shaping Europe’s future

One former trainee described the experience as an opportunity to create and manage a project independently while developing connections and gaining first-hand exposure to the work of a public institution.

Another emphasized continuous learning, humanity and active engagement during the traineeship.

These experiences demonstrate that the programme can be valuable for applicants from a wide range of academic and professional backgrounds.

Application Tips for Prospective Applicants

A strong application should be carefully prepared rather than submitted at the last minute.

1. Research the CoR

Understand the institution’s role in EU policymaking and the importance of local and regional perspectives.

2. Choose Departments Strategically

Since Cicero applicants can select up to three preferred departments, candidates should choose departments that genuinely match their academic and professional interests.

3. Demonstrate Relevant Skills

Highlight experience in areas such as:

  • Research
  • Policy analysis
  • Communication
  • Administration
  • Project management
  • Public affairs
  • European studies
  • International relations
  • Local governance
  • Regional development

4. Check the Language Requirements

Make sure you satisfy the EU-language and English/French requirements before submitting an application.

5. Be Accurate

Do not provide information that cannot be verified.

The CoR explicitly warns that false statements can result in rejection or cancellation.

6. Apply Early

Do not wait until the deadline.

The institution warns that high traffic near the closing time could prevent an application from reaching the system successfully.

7. Check Previous EU Experience

Applicants who have already completed more than eight weeks of an in-house placement with a European institution, body, delegation or representative office, or who have been employed by a European institution or body, may be ineligible for the Cicero programme.

Important Deadlines at a Glance

Because the CoR operates different schemes and two Cicero sessions, there is not one single annual deadline for every opportunity.

Cicero Spring Session

  • Traineeship: 16 February–15 July
  • Applications: 1 July–1 October of the previous year
  • Deadline: 1 October at 12:00 noon Brussels time

Cicero Autumn Session

  • Traineeship: 16 September–15 February
  • Applications: 6 January–31 March
  • Deadline: 31 March at 12:00 noon Brussels time

Study Visits

The source information does not provide one universal annual deadline for study visits. Applicants should use the official application system and check the current availability and applicable arrangements.

Government Official Study Visits

The source information similarly does not specify one universal annual application deadline. Interested public authorities and officials should consult the official CoR application process.

How to Access the Official Application

Applications for the CoR opportunities are submitted through the institution’s online application forms.

Cicero traineeship application:
Apply for a traineeship

Study visit application:
Apply for a study visit

Government official study visit application:
Apply for a study visit for government officials

Applicants should always verify the application scheme they are selecting before submitting their form.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the European Committee of the Regions traineeship paid?

Yes. The Cicero traineeship provides a grant of approximately €1,538 per month, together with travel and mobility allowances. Accident insurance is included, while health insurance coverage is optional.

The study visit and government official study visit schemes are unpaid.

Where is the traineeship located?

The opportunities described here are based at the European Committee of the Regions in Brussels, Belgium.

How long is the Cicero traineeship?

The Cicero traineeship lasts five months and requires full-time participation of 40 hours per week.

Can non-EU citizens apply?

Yes, but under restricted circumstances. Third-country nationals, including UK citizens, may be selected exceptionally if their candidature is of particular interest to the CoR and they satisfy Belgian immigration and legal residence/work requirements.

Do I need a Master’s degree?

No. The Cicero programme requires applicants to have completed a full undergraduate academic degree or at least the third year of higher education by the application deadline.

Can current university students apply?

Yes, provided they have completed at least the third year of higher education by the application deadline.

What languages are required?

Candidates must be fluent in one EU language and have satisfactory knowledge of either English or French.

Can I submit multiple applications?

No. Applicants may submit only one application per traineeship period.

Can I change my application after submitting it?

Applicants can make changes to their form before the relevant application deadline.

What happens if I provide false information?

False statements can result in rejection or cancellation of the traineeship.

Are study visits funded?

Study visits are not funded in the same way as the Cicero traineeship. Applicants must provide proof of funding from another organization, such as a university, public or private body or NGO, or demonstrate that the visit is an integral part of their education.

Are government official study visits paid?

No. Government official study visits are unpaid, with expenses covered by the participant or sending authority.

Visit HERE to learn more about the European Committee of the Regions Traineeships 2026–2027 in Brussels, Belgium.

Official Source and Further Information

For the most current eligibility requirements, application dates, departments, rules and application procedures, applicants should consult the official European Committee of the Regions website.

European Committee of the Regions – Traineeships

For questions concerning traineeships, the CoR provides the following contact:

Email: trainee@cor.europa.eu

Candidates with accessibility or special-needs requirements can contact:

Social-Service-CoR@cor.europa.eu

Conclusion

The European Committee of the Regions traineeships and study visit opportunities in Brussels provide an excellent pathway for students, graduates, young professionals and eligible public-sector officials to gain practical exposure to European policymaking and local and regional governance.

The Cicero traineeship is the most substantial of the three opportunities, offering a five-month, full-time placement in Brussels with a grant of approximately €1,538 per month, travel and mobility support, and accident insurance. It is particularly suitable for university graduates and students who have completed at least three years of higher education and who are interested in EU affairs, public policy, regional development, communication, administration or related fields.

The study visit programme provides students and researchers with a shorter opportunity to complement academic work through first-hand exposure to the CoR, while the government official study visit enables staff and trainees from public authorities in EU Member States to strengthen institutional cooperation and professional networks.

Applicants should pay close attention to the different eligibility requirements, nationality rules, academic qualifications, language requirements and previous EU experience restrictions. Most importantly, candidates should apply early and ensure that all information submitted is accurate.

For the Cicero programme, applicants should remember the two principal annual application windows: 1 July to 1 October at 12:00 noon Brussels time for the Spring Session and 6 January to 31 March at 12:00 noon Brussels time for the Autumn Session.

For students, graduates and public-sector professionals seeking meaningful experience within an EU institution, the European Committee of the Regions represents a valuable opportunity to develop professional skills, build international networks and gain a deeper understanding of how European policies connect with cities and regions.

The Council’s Emerging Leaders Program offers an opportunity for exceptional professionals in Chicago to strengthen their leadership skills, deepen their understanding of U.S. foreign policy and global affairs, and become part of a long-term network of influential leaders.

The Class of 2027 will bring together 20 of Chicago’s promising and accomplished leaders for a rigorous, yearlong experience designed to connect global perspectives with local action.

About the Emerging Leaders Program

The Emerging Leaders Program is designed for professionals who are already making an impact in their respective fields and want to expand their knowledge, leadership capabilities, and professional networks.

For one year, a select group of 20 participants will take part in an intensive program focused on:

  • U.S. foreign policy
  • Global affairs
  • Leadership development
  • Cross-sector networking
  • Global perspectives and local action

Participants come from a wide range of professional backgrounds and organizations across Chicago.

The program brings together leaders from sectors including:

  • Finance
  • Law
  • Healthcare
  • Manufacturing
  • Government
  • Education
  • Arts
  • Nonprofit organizations

This diversity creates an environment where participants can exchange ideas across industries while developing a broader understanding of global issues.

Class of 2027

Applications are currently open for the 2027 Emerging Leaders class.

The program typically selects 20 of Chicago’s best and brightest professionals, generally between the ages of 30 and 45, who demonstrate strong professional achievement and an interest in global affairs and leadership.

The selected participants will spend a year developing their understanding of international issues while strengthening relationships with other accomplished professionals across Chicago.

What Participants Will Gain

The Emerging Leaders Program is designed to provide participants with both knowledge and long-term professional connections.

1. Greater Understanding of Global Affairs

Participants will have the opportunity to deepen their knowledge of U.S. foreign policy and global affairs, helping them better understand international developments and their implications for Chicago and the wider world.

2. Leadership Development

The program focuses on strengthening leadership skills among professionals who are already making significant contributions within their organizations and communities.

Participants can use the experience to develop their ability to think strategically, engage with complex global issues, and contribute to meaningful conversations.

3. Cross-Sector Networking

One of the major features of the program is the opportunity to connect with exceptional professionals from different industries.

Participants become part of a community that brings together leaders from business, government, education, healthcare, law, nonprofits, the arts, and other sectors.

4. Lifelong Professional Connections

Completing the yearlong program gives participants access to a broader community of Council Emerging Leaders.

Rather than ending when the program concludes, these relationships can continue through the Council’s alumni network and wider community.

5. Continued Engagement and Impact

After completing the program, Emerging Leaders become part of a premier alumni network and can continue engaging with the Council.

The program is therefore designed not simply as a one-year leadership experience, but as a pathway toward continued professional connection and participation in conversations shaping the global future.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The program is particularly relevant to professionals who:

  • Are based in Chicago.
  • Are established and exceptional in their professional fields.
  • Typically fall within the 30–45 age range.
  • Have an interest in U.S. foreign policy and global affairs.
  • Want to strengthen their leadership capabilities.
  • Value cross-sector collaboration and networking.
  • Are interested in connecting global issues with local action.
  • Want to become part of a long-term community of influential Chicago leaders.

The information provided specifically describes the program as being for Chicago-based leaders and does not state a particular nationality, race, or citizenship requirement.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

Applications for the Class of 2027 will be accepted until:

September 1, 2026, at 12:00 noon CST

Applicants should ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated deadline.

How to Apply

Interested candidates can submit their applications through the official application portal.

Why This Program Matters

Chicago is home to professionals working across some of the most influential sectors of society. However, addressing major global challenges requires leaders who can look beyond their individual industries and understand how international developments affect communities, businesses, institutions, and governments.

The Emerging Leaders Program provides a platform for professionals from different backgrounds to develop that broader perspective.

By combining global affairs education, leadership development, professional networking, and long-term alumni engagement, the program aims to create a community of leaders capable of contributing to Chicago while maintaining a strong understanding of the wider world.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Emerging Leaders Program 2027

Conclusion

The Emerging Leaders Program Class of 2027 is an opportunity for accomplished Chicago professionals to expand their knowledge of global affairs, strengthen their leadership skills, and build lasting relationships with other influential leaders across the city.

With only 20 participants selected for the program, prospective applicants should carefully prepare their applications and demonstrate how their professional experience, leadership potential, and global outlook align with the program.

Applications close on September 1, 2026, at noon CST. Interested Chicago professionals should submit their applications before the deadline to be considered for the Class of 2027.

Introduction

Making the right academic or career decision can be challenging, particularly when you are navigating scholarships, postgraduate admissions, competitive fellowships, career transitions, job applications, personal branding, or opportunities in another country.

Future of Work Africa (FOWA) has introduced a range of personalised advisory services designed to provide students, young professionals, emerging leaders, scholarship applicants, postgraduate candidates, and career changers with practical guidance for their next academic or professional move.

The advisory services are intended to go beyond general career advice. Depending on the package selected, applicants can receive one-to-one mentorship, career planning, CV and LinkedIn guidance, interview preparation, postgraduate programme recommendations, scholarship matching, application support, statement of purpose review, personal-branding strategy, mock interviews, leadership development, and longer-term career planning.

FOWA states that its opportunity listings and resources remain free, while its advisory services provide paid, personalised support for individuals who want more direct guidance.

Whether you are a university student preparing for your first application, a professional seeking a career transition, a scholarship applicant looking for suitable funding opportunities, or an emerging leader pursuing highly competitive programmes, FOWA’s advisory packages are structured around different stages and goals.

What Is Future of Work Africa (FOWA)?

Future of Work Africa is a social enterprise based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, focused on equipping African youth with knowledge, guidance, and resources for the changing world of work.

The organisation provides access to opportunities and resources while also offering advisory services for people seeking assistance with academic and career decisions.

Its advisory offering is particularly relevant to individuals who may need help turning broad ambitions into a structured application or career strategy.

The services cover areas including:

  • Career direction and goal setting
  • Scholarship identification
  • Postgraduate programme selection
  • Fellowship and leadership-programme applications
  • CV development and review
  • LinkedIn and personal-branding guidance
  • Interview preparation
  • Application planning
  • Statement of Purpose review
  • Career-transition planning
  • Leadership development
  • AI and future-of-work coaching
  • Long-term academic and career planning

FOWA also provides personalised recommendations based on an applicant’s goals and stage.

FOWA Advisory Services: Who Can Benefit?

The advisory services are designed for a broad range of students, professionals, applicants, and emerging leaders.

They may be particularly useful for:

  • University students who need career direction.
  • Recent graduates preparing for their first professional opportunities.
  • Young professionals seeking career advancement.
  • Individuals transitioning into a new career field.
  • Scholarship applicants looking for suitable funding opportunities.
  • Students seeking Master’s or doctoral programmes.
  • Candidates preparing applications for highly competitive fellowships.
  • Applicants targeting leadership programmes.
  • Chevening applicants.
  • Mastercard Foundation Scholars applicants.
  • Rhodes Scholarship applicants.
  • McCall MacBain Scholarship applicants.
  • Entrepreneurs and emerging leaders.
  • Professionals seeking stronger personal branding.
  • Applicants who want support preparing competitive applications.
  • Individuals who need help developing a structured academic or career plan.

FOWA Compass — TZS 30,000

The FOWA Compass package is positioned as an entry-level advisory service for individuals who need practical, personalised guidance.

The listed price is TZS 30,000.

This package can be particularly useful for university students, young professionals, first-time applicants, and people who are uncertain about their next academic or career step.

What the FOWA Compass package includes

The package includes:

  1. One-to-one mentorship session

    Applicants receive personalised attention rather than relying exclusively on general online resources.

  2. Career direction and goal setting

    The service helps applicants clarify their professional direction and establish goals that can guide their next steps.

  3. CV or LinkedIn guidance

    Applicants can receive guidance on improving either their CV or LinkedIn presence.

  4. Interview preparation guidance

    Candidates can receive advice on preparing for interviews and presenting themselves more effectively.

  5. Relevant opportunity recommendations

    FOWA can recommend opportunities that align with the applicant’s goals and circumstances.

  6. Application assistance to two job or internship opportunities

    The package includes assistance with applications to up to two job or internship opportunities.

  7. Personalised action plan

    Applicants receive a structured plan outlining practical steps to take after the advisory session.

Who is the Compass package best for?

FOWA identifies this package as particularly suitable for:

  • University students
  • Young professionals
  • First-time applicants

It can therefore serve as a starting point for individuals who need clarity before investing in a more extensive advisory programme.

FOWA Pinnacle — Postgraduate and Scholarship Advisory

The Pinnacle package is designed for individuals pursuing postgraduate education, scholarships, or study-abroad opportunities.

This service is particularly relevant to applicants who need help identifying suitable Master’s or doctoral programmes and matching their academic goals with potential scholarships.

What the Pinnacle package includes

The package provides support in several important areas.

1. Master’s or doctoral programme identification

FOWA can assist applicants in identifying postgraduate programmes that align with their academic background and future goals.

2. Shortlisting of up to five universities or programmes

Applicants can receive a shortlist containing up to five relevant universities or programmes.

This can help reduce the amount of time spent researching institutions independently.

3. Matching with up to five scholarships

FOWA can identify up to five scholarship opportunities that may be relevant to the applicant.

Scholarship matching can be particularly valuable because funding opportunities often have different eligibility requirements, application procedures, deadlines, and selection criteria.

4. Application planning

Applicants receive guidance on how to organise their application process and approach the requirements systematically.

5. General visa-pathway information

The package includes general information concerning possible visa pathways.

However, this should not be interpreted as professional immigration or legal advice.

6. Statement of Purpose review

Applicants can receive a review of their Statement of Purpose, an important component of many postgraduate applications.

7. CV review

FOWA can review the applicant’s CV and provide guidance relevant to postgraduate or scholarship applications.

8. Review of up to two application documents

The package includes review of up to two application documents, with up to two revision rounds.

Who is Pinnacle best for?

The package is intended particularly for:

  • Postgraduate applicants
  • Scholarship applicants
  • Study-abroad candidates

For applicants who are uncertain about which universities, programmes, or scholarships to pursue, this package provides a more structured approach to postgraduate planning.

FOWA Select — Fellowship, Leadership and Career-Transition Support

FOWA also offers a service focused on competitive fellowships, leadership programmes, personal branding, and career transitions.

This package is particularly relevant to individuals pursuing prestigious or highly competitive opportunities where the quality and strategic positioning of an application can be important.

What the package includes

Fellowship and leadership-programme application support

Applicants can receive guidance while preparing applications for fellowships and leadership programmes.

Personal-branding strategy

The service includes support for developing a stronger professional identity and personal brand.

This may be useful for applicants who need to communicate their experience, leadership potential, professional interests, and future goals more effectively.

Career-transition planning

Professionals considering a move into another sector, industry, profession, or career path can receive structured guidance for the transition.

Scholarship and fellowship coaching

Applicants can receive coaching specifically focused on competitive scholarship and fellowship applications.

Support for up to two competitive applications

The package provides support for up to two competitive applications.

Review of up to four application documents

Applicants can receive reviews of up to four application documents, with up to two revision rounds per document.

Up to two mock interviews

Candidates can practise interview scenarios through up to two mock interviews.

Who is this package best for?

FOWA specifically identifies the service as suitable for applicants pursuing programmes such as:

  • Chevening
  • Mastercard Foundation Scholars
  • Rhodes
  • McCall MacBain

It may also benefit applicants pursuing other selective scholarships, fellowships, and leadership programmes.

FOWA Legacy — Future Package Coming Soon

FOWA lists FOWA Legacy as a future package.

The advertised starting price is TZS 350,000+, with support extending for up to three months.

The package is designed for individuals seeking a longer-term and more structured mentorship relationship.

What FOWA Legacy is expected to include

The package is listed as including everything in Pinnacle, in addition to:

  • Personalised mentorship
  • AI and future-of-work coaching
  • Leadership development
  • Monthly progress reviews
  • Networking opportunities
  • Support for up to four applications
  • Review of up to eight application documents
  • Up to three revision rounds per document
  • Up to three mock interviews
  • Priority booking

Who is FOWA Legacy best for?

FOWA identifies the package as particularly suitable for:

  • Emerging leaders
  • Entrepreneurs
  • High-achieving students
  • High-achieving professionals

The concept behind the package is long-term development rather than assistance with a single application.

FOWA presents this service under the message of building a legacy that can inspire future generations.

What Makes the FOWA Advisory Services Different?

One of the main features of the service is its personalised approach.

Instead of providing only generic information about scholarships, jobs, universities, or fellowships, the advisory model is structured around an individual’s goals and current stage.

Depending on the selected package, applicants can receive assistance with:

  • Identifying suitable opportunities
  • Understanding their career direction
  • Choosing postgraduate programmes
  • Finding potential scholarships
  • Preparing applications
  • Improving application documents
  • Preparing for interviews
  • Developing personal brands
  • Planning career transitions
  • Developing leadership capabilities
  • Creating longer-term academic and professional plans

This can be especially valuable for applicants who feel overwhelmed by the number of opportunities available online and need help determining which ones are genuinely relevant to them.

How the FOWA Booking Process Works

FOWA has outlined a six-step process for accessing its advisory services.

Step 1: Select a package

Applicants first select the advisory package that best matches their needs.

Options range from the entry-level Compass package to more extensive services.

Step 2: Complete the form

Applicants provide their information and submit three preferred times for the session.

This enables FOWA to understand the applicant’s needs and determine availability.

Step 3: Receive a reference

FOWA confirms availability and provides a reference for the booking.

Applicants should retain this reference because it is used during subsequent payment and confirmation steps.

Step 4: Make payment

Payment should only be made after the booking request has been confirmed.

FOWA specifically advises applicants not to make payments before confirmation.

Step 5: Send payment proof

Applicants send proof of payment through WhatsApp using the reference provided.

A copy of the payment receipt can also be attached through the registration process.

Step 6: Receive confirmation

Once the payment has been verified, the meeting details are sent to the applicant.

Payment Information

FOWA states that payments are currently processed through Simon Swale, the authorised FOWA representative.

An official payment acknowledgement is issued after verification.

The organisation specifically warns applicants to use only the payment information displayed on the official FOWA website and not to send money to any other number.

Important Terms and Conditions

Applicants should understand the service limitations before making a booking.

FOWA provides several important clarifications.

“Up to” means the maximum support included

When FOWA states that a package includes “up to” a particular number of applications, documents, sessions, or mock interviews, this represents the maximum level of support available under that package.

It does not necessarily mean that every applicant will require or use every component.

Services depend on the applicant’s goals and stage

The exact support provided can depend on the applicant’s individual circumstances, objectives, and stage of development.

No rollover or refund

FOWA states that services must be used within the applicable package period.

Unused services do not roll over, and the listed terms state that there are no refunds.

No guaranteed outcome

Applicants should not interpret the advisory service as a guarantee of:

  • University admission
  • Scholarship funding
  • Fellowship selection
  • Employment
  • Visa approval

Selection decisions ultimately remain with the relevant university, employer, scholarship provider, fellowship organisation, or immigration authority.

Visa guidance is general

The visa component provides general pathway information only.

FOWA states that it is not legal or immigration advice.

Applicants who require professional immigration or legal advice should consult appropriately qualified professionals.

Application and Registration Process

The registration interface allows applicants to select their preferred service and provide their details.

For the Compass service, the listed selection is:

FOWA Compass — TZS 30,000

Applicants are asked to provide:

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • WhatsApp number
  • Country
  • A description of what they want to achieve
  • Payment receipt

The form allows applicants to explain their objectives in up to 1,000 characters.

Proof of payment is required before the registration can be submitted.

Applicants can also send a copy of their payment receipt through WhatsApp.

APPLY HERE

Response Time aAvailability

FOWA states that advisory enquiries are reviewed:

  • Monday to Friday
  • East Africa Time (EAT)
  • With a response expected within one business day

The services are available online or in person in Dar es Salaam.

This gives applicants outside Tanzania the option of accessing the advisory services remotely.

FOWA’s Free Opportunities and Resources

It is important to distinguish FOWA’s paid advisory services from its wider opportunity platform.

FOWA states that its:

  • Opportunity listings
  • Resources
  • Curated information

remain free.

The paid component is the personalised advisory service.

This means individuals who do not require one-to-one assistance can still make use of FOWA’s free opportunity and resource content.

Newsletter and Opportunity Updates

FOWA also offers newsletter subscriptions for individuals interested in receiving curated information about opportunities.

The newsletter covers areas such as:

  • Scholarships
  • Fellowships
  • Jobs
  • Resources
  • Future-of-Work insights

Applicants can select between:

  • Weekly digest
  • Monthly digest

The organisation states that subscribers can unsubscribe at any time.

Who Can Apply or Use the FOWA Advisory Services?

The advisory services are broadly targeted at students, professionals, emerging leaders, scholarship applicants, postgraduate applicants, fellowship applicants, entrepreneurs, and individuals undergoing career transitions.

The listed services are not presented as being restricted to one nationality.

FOWA is based in Tanzania and provides services online or in Dar es Salaam, meaning individuals outside Tanzania can potentially access the services remotely.

The international payment information also explicitly refers to international students.

Geographic eligibility

The service is oriented toward African youth and professionals, but the provided information does not establish a restrictive nationality or continental eligibility rule for purchasing advisory services.

Applicants from outside Tanzania can therefore contact FOWA for relevant international arrangements.

Race and ethnicity

The information provided does not specify any race-based restriction.

Academic and professional background

Eligibility depends largely on the service selected and the applicant’s goals.

Relevant groups include:

  • Current university students
  • Graduates
  • Young professionals
  • Career changers
  • Postgraduate applicants
  • Scholarship applicants
  • Study-abroad candidates
  • Fellowship applicants
  • Leadership-programme applicants
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Emerging leaders
  • High-achieving students and professionals

Opportunity Category

Category: Career and Academic Advisory Service / Professional Mentorship

This is not a scholarship, fellowship, grant, internship, job, competition, conference, or award. It is a paid advisory and mentorship service supporting academic applications, scholarships, fellowships, career development, and professional transitions.

Deadline

No specific application deadline is stated in the information provided.

The services appear to operate on an ongoing booking basis, subject to availability.

FOWA states that enquiries are reviewed Monday to Friday during East Africa Time and that responses are expected within one business day.

Applicants should therefore check the official FOWA platform for current availability before making payment.

Why Applicants Should Consider Personalised Advisory Support

Applying for scholarships, postgraduate programmes, jobs, and fellowships can require significant research and preparation.

A personalised advisory service can help applicants avoid common mistakes such as:

  • Applying randomly to unsuitable opportunities.
  • Missing important application requirements.
  • Submitting generic personal statements.
  • Using an unfocused CV.
  • Failing to communicate career goals clearly.
  • Choosing programmes that do not align with long-term objectives.
  • Applying for scholarships without checking eligibility.
  • Entering interviews without adequate preparation.
  • Attempting a career transition without a structured plan.

FOWA’s packages are structured to address different levels of these needs.

For someone who simply needs career clarity, Compass may be appropriate. For a postgraduate applicant, Pinnacle provides more specialised support. For highly competitive fellowship and leadership applications, the Select service offers more extensive application and interview support. Legacy is positioned for applicants seeking longer-term mentorship.

How to Choose the Right FOWA Package

Applicants should consider their primary objective before selecting a package.

Choose Compass if:

  • You are unsure about your career direction.
  • You are a first-time applicant.
  • You need CV or LinkedIn guidance.
  • You want interview preparation.
  • You need recommendations for jobs or internships.
  • You need a personalised action plan.

Choose Pinnacle if:

  • You are planning a Master’s or PhD.
  • You need help identifying universities.
  • You are looking for scholarships.
  • You are planning to study abroad.
  • You need help with a Statement of Purpose.
  • You want your postgraduate application documents reviewed.

Choose Select if:

  • You are applying for a competitive fellowship.
  • You are targeting a leadership programme.
  • You are applying for Chevening, Rhodes, Mastercard Foundation Scholars, McCall MacBain, or similar programmes.
  • You need personal-branding support.
  • You are changing careers.
  • You need mock interviews.
  • You want support with multiple competitive applications.

Consider Legacy when available if:

  • You want long-term mentorship.
  • You are an emerging leader.
  • You are an entrepreneur.
  • You are a high-achieving student or professional.
  • You want leadership development.
  • You need continued career planning.
  • You want AI and future-of-work coaching.

Important Advice Before Paying

Applicants should carefully follow the payment instructions.

The information provided by FOWA specifically states that payment should be made only after the booking request has been confirmed.

A sensible process is therefore:

  1. Select the appropriate package.
  2. Submit the booking request.
  3. Provide your preferred times.
  4. Wait for confirmation.
  5. Receive your booking reference.
  6. Verify the payment details.
  7. Make the payment.
  8. Save the receipt.
  9. Send proof of payment through the specified channel.
  10. Wait for final confirmation and meeting details.

Applicants should avoid sending money to unofficial numbers or accounts.

They should also retain all payment evidence and correspondence until the service has been completed.

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Organisation Future of Work Africa (FOWA)
Location Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
Service type Academic and career advisory
Delivery Online or in-person
Response time Within 1 business day
Working days Monday–Friday
Time zone East Africa Time (EAT)
Entry package FOWA Compass — TZS 30,000
Postgraduate package FOWA Pinnacle
Competitive applications FOWA Select
Long-term mentorship FOWA Legacy — coming soon
International access Available through online support
Specific deadline None stated
Opportunity listings Free
Advisory services Paid
Visa support General information only
Admission/funding guarantee None

Conclusion

Future of Work Africa’s advisory services provide a structured option for students, graduates, professionals, scholarship applicants, postgraduate candidates, fellowship applicants, and emerging leaders who want personalised support with their academic and career goals.

Rather than offering one standard service to everyone, FOWA has structured its advisory model around different levels of need. The Compass package focuses on career direction and foundational guidance, while Pinnacle targets postgraduate and scholarship applicants. Select is designed for competitive fellowship, leadership, personal-branding, and career-transition needs, while Legacy is positioned as a longer-term mentorship package for emerging leaders, entrepreneurs, and high-achieving individuals.

The service may be particularly useful for applicants who know where they want to go but need help developing a practical strategy for getting there.

However, applicants should remember that advisory support does not guarantee admission, scholarships, fellowships, employment, or visa approval. Success ultimately depends on the applicant’s qualifications, application quality, competitiveness, and decisions made by the relevant institutions.

With no specific deadline stated, interested applicants can explore the available FOWA advisory options on an ongoing basis, subject to availability. Anyone considering the service should first identify their specific objective, select the package that matches that objective, submit a booking request, wait for confirmation, and only then proceed with payment using the officially provided payment details.

For African students and professionals seeking clearer direction in an increasingly competitive academic and professional environment, FOWA’s personalised advisory model offers an opportunity to combine structured planning with individual mentorship and application support.
