Opportunity Overview

The develoPPP programme, commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), provides financial and technical support to private-sector companies seeking to implement sustainable business projects in developing and emerging countries.

For more than 25 years, develoPPP has supported businesses that combine commercial opportunities with development-policy impact. The programme is designed for companies that want to invest sustainably, expand their activities in developing or emerging markets, strengthen local expertise, improve environmental and social standards, or introduce innovative solutions that contribute to better living conditions.

Through the programme, eligible businesses can receive significant public financial support while also benefiting from technical expertise and access to local networks.

The current develoPPP Classic call for applications is open until September 30, 2026.

What Is the develoPPP Programme?

develoPPP is a development cooperation programme that brings together the interests and capabilities of the private sector and international development cooperation.

The programme recognises that sustainable development cannot be achieved through public-sector action alone. Businesses operating in developing and emerging markets can create jobs, introduce new technologies, develop skills, improve supply chains and provide products and services that address important social and environmental challenges.

develoPPP therefore supports projects where there is both:

  • A genuine business interest for the participating company; and
  • A measurable contribution to sustainable development.

Rather than functioning as a conventional business loan, develoPPP provides public funding and technical support for qualifying development-oriented private-sector projects.

The programme operates in more than 60 countries worldwide, providing companies with opportunities to implement projects in a broad range of emerging and developing markets.

How Much Funding Is Available?

One of the major attractions of develoPPP is the scale of support available.

Under develoPPP Classic, suitable projects can receive up to €2 million in public funding.

The public contribution can cover a maximum of 50% of the total project costs.

This means the participating company must also make a substantial financial contribution to the project. The programme is therefore structured as a partnership in which the private sector and public development cooperation share responsibility for achieving the project’s objectives.

The funding can be particularly valuable for businesses that have a strong development-oriented project but require additional financial resources, technical expertise or local partnerships to implement it effectively.

Who Can Benefit From develoPPP?

The programme is particularly relevant to companies that want to combine commercial expansion with measurable economic, social or environmental benefits.

Potential areas of interest include businesses seeking to:

  1. Expand sustainable operations in an emerging market.
  2. Establish or strengthen local business activities.
  3. Train local employees and develop skilled workers.
  4. Improve working conditions and labour standards.
  5. Strengthen environmental and social standards.
  6. Make international supply chains more transparent and sustainable.
  7. Introduce innovative business models.
  8. Improve living conditions through commercially viable solutions.
  9. Build local expertise and technical capacity.
  10. Develop sustainable production processes.

The programme is not limited to one specific industry. Instead, the suitability of a project depends heavily on whether it meets the programme’s development and business criteria.

develoPPP Classic

New Call for Applications

The current develoPPP Classic call focuses on private-sector initiatives that contribute to the sustainable transformation of economies in developing and emerging countries.

Companies interested in obtaining funding for suitable projects can submit applications to one of the programme’s implementing partners, DEG Impulse or GIZ.

Deadline

September 30, 2026

Companies considering an application should therefore begin preparing their project proposal, supporting documentation and financing information well before the deadline.

What Is develoPPP Classic?

develoPPP Classic is designed for companies that want to invest sustainably in an emerging market and expand their operational activities locally.

The programme can provide qualifying projects with:

  • Financial support of up to €2 million in public funding.
  • Technical support and expertise.
  • Access to local networks.
  • Assistance in addressing development-related challenges.
  • Support for sustainable business expansion.

The emphasis is on projects where the company’s commercial activities can contribute to broader development outcomes.

For example, a company entering or expanding in an emerging market could potentially use a develoPPP-supported project to develop local employees, improve production standards, strengthen environmental performance or introduce a solution addressing a development challenge.

develoPPP Ventures

In addition to develoPPP Classic, the programme offers develoPPP Ventures, which is targeted at younger companies with innovative business models.

This funding instrument is designed for startups and young businesses that are already active in an emerging market and are ready to take their business to the next stage.

Under the matching-funds model, a public early-stage investment of up to €100,000 is possible.

This makes develoPPP Ventures particularly relevant to innovative businesses that have moved beyond the earliest stages of development and are looking for additional capital to scale their operations.

The key distinction between the two instruments is therefore:

Funding Instrument Main Target Group Potential Public Support
develoPPP Classic Companies investing sustainably and expanding operations in emerging markets Up to €2 million
develoPPP Ventures Young companies with innovative business models active in emerging markets Up to €100,000

Selected Focus Area: Sustainable Supply Chains

One of the programme’s highlighted focus areas is sustainable supply chains.

Modern supply chains often involve businesses, suppliers, manufacturers and workers across multiple countries. As consumers, regulators and international markets increasingly demand responsible production, companies are facing growing pressure to understand and improve their supply chains.

The develoPPP programme identifies this challenge as an opportunity for businesses to create positive development impacts while strengthening their own operations.

Companies may be interested in develoPPP support if they want to:

  • Increase supply-chain transparency.
  • Improve sustainability standards.
  • Strengthen oversight of suppliers.
  • Improve production processes.
  • Support compliance with international standards.
  • Improve environmental performance.
  • Strengthen social standards among suppliers.
  • Create more sustainable production systems.

For businesses operating internationally, improving supply-chain sustainability can provide benefits beyond compliance. It can also improve resilience, reputation, product quality and long-term competitiveness.

Selected Focus Area: Vocational Training

Another highlighted area is vocational training and skills development.

Access to appropriately trained workers remains an important challenge for businesses operating internationally, particularly in developing and emerging markets.

Companies may face difficulties finding workers with the technical knowledge and practical skills required for their operations.

At the same time, vocational training can create significant development benefits by improving people’s employability and helping local economies build a stronger skilled workforce.

The develoPPP programme therefore highlights opportunities for companies that want to:

  • Train local workers.
  • Develop skilled employees.
  • Improve technical and professional competencies.
  • Recruit talent fairly.
  • Address local skills gaps.
  • Create pathways into employment.
  • Strengthen the long-term availability of qualified workers.

Businesses interested in expanding in an emerging market may therefore consider incorporating employee training and skills development into their broader investment strategy.

Why the Programme Is Important for Developing and Emerging Markets

The develoPPP model is based on the idea that private-sector investment can contribute substantially to sustainable development.

When businesses invest responsibly in developing and emerging economies, the potential benefits can extend beyond the company itself.

These may include:

Job Creation

Business expansion can create employment opportunities and generate income for local communities.

Skills Development

Training programmes can equip workers with technical and professional skills that remain valuable beyond the individual project.

Improved Standards

Companies can help strengthen environmental, social, labour and production standards within their operations and supply chains.

Technology and Innovation

Businesses can introduce new technologies, products and processes that address local challenges.

Economic Development

Sustainable private investment can contribute to stronger local businesses, supply chains and markets.

Improved Living Conditions

Where projects address important development challenges, commercial activity can contribute to improvements in people’s living conditions.

What Makes a Project Suitable?

A strong develoPPP project should demonstrate a clear relationship between the company’s business objectives and its development impact.

Applicants should therefore consider whether their proposed project can clearly explain:

  1. The business opportunity
    What commercial opportunity is the company pursuing?
  2. The development challenge
    What economic, social or environmental problem does the project address?
  3. The proposed solution
    What activities will the company undertake?
  4. The development impact
    How will the project benefit workers, communities, consumers, suppliers or the wider economy?
  5. The company’s contribution
    What resources will the company provide?
  6. The public contribution
    How would develoPPP funding help make the project possible or significantly improve its scale or impact?
  7. Sustainability
    How will the benefits continue beyond the funding period?
  8. Local relevance
    Why is the project appropriate for the specific developing or emerging market?

Benefits of Participating in develoPPP

For qualifying companies, participation can provide several important advantages.

1. Significant Financial Support

Eligible develoPPP Classic projects can receive up to €2 million in public funding, subject to the programme’s conditions and the maximum public contribution of 50%.

2. Technical Expertise

Companies can benefit not only from funding but also from technical support relevant to development-oriented projects.

3. Local Networks

The programme highlights access to local networks as one of its advantages. This can be particularly valuable for companies entering unfamiliar markets.

4. Support for Sustainable Expansion

Businesses can use the programme to strengthen sustainable operations while expanding in developing and emerging economies.

5. Development Impact

A successful project can generate measurable benefits for workers, suppliers, communities and local economies while supporting the company’s commercial objectives.

6. International Opportunities

With the programme available in more than 60 countries, companies can explore opportunities across a wide geographical range.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The opportunity is primarily intended for private-sector companies, rather than individual applicants.

The exact eligibility requirements depend on the particular develoPPP funding instrument and project. Businesses should therefore review the official programme requirements carefully before submitting an application.

The programme is particularly relevant to:

  • Small and medium-sized enterprises.
  • Larger companies.
  • Young companies and startups with innovative business models, particularly under develoPPP Ventures.
  • Companies already operating in or planning sustainable activities in developing or emerging markets.
  • Businesses seeking to develop local talent and skills.
  • Companies working to improve environmental and social standards.
  • Businesses seeking more sustainable international supply chains.
  • Companies developing innovative solutions with development potential.

The programme is not a scholarship, individual fellowship, internship or conventional employment opportunity. Individuals cannot normally apply simply as individuals for the business funding described here.

Countries and Geographic Eligibility

develoPPP operates internationally and is available in more than 60 developing and emerging countries.

The programme is therefore not restricted to applicants from one particular continent or nationality. However, eligibility is determined according to the programme’s list of eligible countries and the specific requirements applicable to the proposed project.

This means that companies interested in implementing projects in Africa, Asia, Latin America and other eligible developing or emerging markets should verify whether their intended project location is covered by the relevant develoPPP instrument.

For applicants from Ghana and other African countries, the most important consideration is not simply nationality. The proposed business project and its intended country of implementation must satisfy the applicable programme requirements.

Companies should therefore confirm the current eligible-country and project criteria directly through the official develoPPP programme before investing substantial time in an application.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity could be particularly relevant to a company that can answer “yes” to several of the following questions:

  • Does your company want to expand into or strengthen its activities in an emerging market?
  • Are you planning a sustainable investment project?
  • Do you want to train local employees?
  • Are you addressing a shortage of skilled workers?
  • Do you want to improve environmental standards?
  • Are you working to improve social standards?
  • Do you want to make your supply chain more sustainable?
  • Does your business have an innovative solution that could improve living conditions?
  • Can the project generate both commercial and development benefits?
  • Is your company prepared to contribute financially to the project?

If several of these apply, develoPPP may be worth investigating further.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Companies should avoid treating the application simply as a request for money. The strength of the proposal will depend on how convincingly the project connects business interests with sustainable development impact.

A strong preparation process should include the following steps:

Step 1: Define the Business Problem

Clearly explain what the company wants to achieve commercially and why the project is important.

Step 2: Identify the Development Challenge

Explain the broader challenge affecting workers, communities, suppliers, consumers or the local economy.

Step 3: Design the Project

Set out the activities, timeline, location, beneficiaries and expected outcomes.

Step 4: Establish Measurable Results

Where possible, identify measurable indicators such as:

  • Number of people trained.
  • Number of jobs created.
  • Number of suppliers reached.
  • Reduction in environmental impacts.
  • Number of workers benefiting from improved standards.
  • Improvements in production efficiency.
  • Number of businesses or communities reached.

Step 5: Prepare the Financial Model

Clearly establish:

  • Total project cost.
  • Company’s financial contribution.
  • Requested public contribution.
  • Other financing sources, where applicable.
  • Expected use of funds.

Because the public contribution under develoPPP Classic can cover a maximum of 50% of project costs, companies should be prepared to demonstrate their own financial commitment.

Step 6: Demonstrate Sustainability

Explain how the project will continue generating benefits after the public funding ends.

Step 7: Review the Eligibility Requirements

Before submitting, carefully check the official requirements for the applicable funding instrument and intended project country.

Application Deadline

The current develoPPP Classic call for applications closes on September 30, 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final days to begin preparing their proposals. Business projects involving international operations, financial contributions, development indicators and implementation partners can require significant preparation.

Official programme: develoPPP – German development cooperation with the private sector

All information on the funding programme, current project examples  and the conditions of participation can be found on the programme website www.develoPPP.de

Visit the OFY Website HERE for more funding programmes

Early preparation allows companies to:

  • Confirm eligibility.
  • Develop a realistic project concept.
  • Prepare financial information.
  • Identify implementation partners.
  • Establish measurable development objectives.
  • Collect supporting documents.
  • Address potential weaknesses before submission.

Programme Partners and Implementation

The develoPPP programmer is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

The programme is implemented through development and financial-sector partners, including:

  • GIZ – Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
  • DEG Impulse gGmbH

The programme’s official information also provides separate contacts for general questions and for questions concerning concrete projects.

For general questions concerning develoPPP or other BMZ funding programmes, the programme lists Hans-Joachim Hebgen, Senior Consultant at the Agency for Business & Economic Development.

For questions concerning concrete projects, applicants can contact the relevant implementing partner.

The official programme lists:

DEG Impulse gGmbH
Daniel Thomann, Head of Programme
Email: develoPPP@degimpulse.de

GIZ GmbH
Anja Meinecke, Head of Programme
Jonas Naguib, Head of Programme
Email: develoPPP@giz.de

Important Things Applicants Should Understand

Before applying, businesses should keep several points in mind.

This Is Business Funding

develoPPP is designed for private-sector activities. It is not a general personal grant for individuals.

Development Impact Matters

A project must demonstrate more than commercial potential. Its contribution to sustainable development is an important part of the programme’s purpose.

Co-Financing Is Required

For develoPPP Classic, public funding can cover a maximum of 50% of the project costs. Companies therefore need to demonstrate their own financial participation.

Country Eligibility Matters

Not every country or project will necessarily qualify under every funding instrument. Applicants should verify the current rules for their intended location.

Funding Is Not Automatic

Meeting the general description of the programme does not guarantee funding. Projects must be assessed against the relevant programme requirements.

develoPPP Classic vs develoPPP Ventures

Although both instruments operate under the wider develoPPP programme, they address somewhat different business situations.

develoPPP Classic is more appropriate for companies seeking to implement substantial sustainable investment projects and expand their operational activities in emerging markets. It can provide up to €2 million in public funding.

develoPPP Ventures focuses on young companies with innovative business models that are active in an emerging market and ready for their next stage of development. Under its matching-funds model, a public early-stage investment of €100,000 is possible.

Businesses should therefore determine which instrument best matches their stage of development, business model and proposed project.

Why Companies Should Explore This Opportunity

The combination of financial support, technical expertise and local networks makes develoPPP particularly relevant to companies that want to enter or expand within developing and emerging markets responsibly.

Rather than viewing development and business growth as separate objectives, the programme encourages companies to design projects where both can reinforce each other.

For example, a company can potentially expand its operations while simultaneously training local workers, improving supplier standards, strengthening environmental performance or introducing solutions that address local needs.

This creates a model in which private-sector investment can contribute to broader economic and social progress.

Conclusion

The develoPPP programme offers an important opportunity for companies seeking to combine sustainable business investment with measurable development impact in developing and emerging markets.

Through develoPPP Classic, eligible projects can receive up to €2 million in public funding, with the public contribution limited to a maximum of 50% of project costs. Companies can also benefit from technical support and local networks.

The programme’s highlighted areas, including sustainable supply chains and vocational training, demonstrate the broad range of projects that can potentially connect commercial objectives with development priorities.

For younger innovative businesses, develoPPP Ventures provides a separate pathway, with a public early-stage investment of up to €100,000 under a matching-funds model.

With opportunities available across more than 60 countries, develoPPP can be particularly valuable to businesses that are serious about sustainable international expansion, skills development, responsible supply chains, environmental and social standards, and innovative solutions to development challenges.

Companies interested in the current develoPPP Classic call should begin preparing early and ensure that their proposed project meets the programme’s detailed requirements.

Deadline: September 30, 2026.

For complete eligibility requirements, application procedures, country information and official programme guidance, applicants should consult the official develoPPP website before submitting a project.

Introduction

Universities around the world are increasingly expanding their academic programs in Korean Studies and Korean language education in response to growing global interest in Korea, its language, culture, economy, politics, history, society, and international relations.

To support this global development, the Korea Foundation (KF) has opened applications for its 2027 Support for Establishment of Professorship program. The initiative provides financial support to universities outside the Republic of Korea that intend to establish a new professorship in Korean Studies or Korean Language.

The program is designed not simply to provide short-term funding, but to help universities create sustainable academic positions that can contribute to the long-term development of Korean Studies and Korean language education in their respective regions.

Under the program, selected universities can receive support toward the establishment of either a tenure-track position or an endowed chair position. Depending on the type of position, the Korea Foundation can provide substantial financial assistance toward salary, employee benefits, or an endowment, while the recipient university is expected to demonstrate a strong institutional commitment to maintaining the professorship beyond the Korea Foundation’s initial support.

The application period runs from July 1 to September 11, 2026, with the application deadline set for September 11, 2026, at 18:00 Korea Standard Time (KST).

This article explains the opportunity in detail, including who can apply, the available funding, eligible academic areas, requirements, application documents, evaluation criteria, important conditions, and the expected timeline.

2027 Support for Establishment of Professorship at a Glance

  • Program: 2027 Support for Establishment of Professorship
  • Organizer: Korea Foundation
  • Opportunity type: Institutional grant
  • Eligible applicants: Universities outside the Republic of Korea
  • Eligible academic fields: Korean Studies and Korean Language
  • Purpose: Establishment of new Korean Studies or Korean Language professorships
  • Available position types: Tenure-track Position and Endowed Chair Position
  • Grant period: Three to five years
  • Application opening: July 1, 2026
  • Application deadline: September 11, 2026
  • Deadline time: 18:00 KST
  • Results announcement: December 2026
  • Expected grant commencement: 2027-28 or 2028-29 academic year
  • Application language: Korean or English
  • Application platform: Korea Foundation Online Application System

What Is the Korea Foundation’s Support for Establishment of Professorship Program?

The Korea Foundation’s Support for Establishment of Professorship program is intended to help universities outside Korea strengthen their capacity to teach and conduct research in Korean Studies and Korean language.

The program focuses specifically on the creation of new professorships rather than simply funding existing positions.

The Korea Foundation seeks to support universities that have the necessary academic infrastructure and demonstrate sufficient potential for the continued growth and development of Korean Studies.

A major feature of the program is its emphasis on sustainability.

The Korea Foundation’s funding is intended to help establish the position, but the recipient university is expected to have a long-term plan for maintaining the professorship after the initial Korea Foundation support ends.

This means that universities applying should not view the program as a temporary source of salary funding. Instead, they should demonstrate how the newly established professorship will become a permanent part of the university’s academic structure.

The program supports two principal models:

  1. Tenure-Track Position
  2. Endowed Chair Position

Who Can Apply?

The primary applicants are universities outside the Republic of Korea that plan to create a new professorship in Korean Studies or Korean Language.

This distinction is important because the opportunity is not designed for individual applicants seeking personal funding.

An individual cannot apply independently for the professorship establishment grant.

Instead, the application must come from an eligible university that intends to establish a new academic position.

The applicant institution should have appropriate infrastructure and demonstrate the ability and commitment to develop Korean Studies or Korean language education and research.

The Korea Foundation will consider factors such as:

  • The university’s existing Korean Studies activities
  • Current faculty members working in Korean Studies or Korean language
  • Existing Korean Studies or Korean language courses
  • Library collections and academic resources
  • Previous academic activities
  • The university’s reputation and experience
  • The institution’s long-term development plans
  • Its ability to support the proposed professorship
  • The feasibility of the proposed project
  • The university’s financial commitment to the position

Eligible Academic Areas

The program supports new professorships in two closely related academic areas:

1. Korean Studies

Korean Studies encompasses academic research and teaching relating to Korea. Depending on the university’s academic structure, this may include areas such as:

  • Korean history
  • Korean politics
  • Korean society
  • Korean culture
  • Korean economics
  • Korean international relations
  • Korean literature
  • Korean philosophy
  • Korean sociology
  • Korean anthropology
  • Korean media and communications
  • Korean regional studies
  • Interdisciplinary Korean Studies

The proposed position should have a meaningful focus on Korea and contribute to the university’s Korean Studies program.

2. Korean Language

Universities may also seek support for the establishment of a new professorship focused on Korean language.

This can strengthen:

  • Korean language teaching
  • Korean language research
  • Korean language curriculum development
  • Korean language academic programs
  • Korean language scholarship
  • Advanced Korean language education
  • Research using Korean-language sources

The university must demonstrate how the proposed professorship will contribute to the development of Korean language education and/or research at the institution.

What Funding Is Available?

The Korea Foundation provides support through two different professorship models.

1. Tenure-Track Position

For a new tenure-track position, the Korea Foundation can provide up to 70% of the total amount of the professor’s salary and employee benefits.

The salary is based on the salary structure already established by the recipient university.

This means the Korea Foundation does not simply impose a universal salary amount on every institution. Instead, the relevant professor’s compensation is determined according to the existing professor salary scale of the university.

Employee benefits

The program also recognizes employee benefits as part of the support.

These are non-wage payments and employment-related costs that an employer is legally required to provide to employees under the laws and regulations applicable in the state or country where the university is located.

The Korea Foundation can therefore contribute toward both the professor’s salary and eligible employee benefits, subject to the program’s funding arrangements and the final grant agreement.

Important sustainability requirement

The university must be prepared to continuously maintain the tenure-track position using its own resources after the Korea Foundation’s initial support ends.

This is one of the most important elements of the program.

Universities should therefore have a credible financial and institutional plan showing how the position will become sustainable over the long term.

2. Endowed Chair Position

The second option is an Endowed Chair Position.

Under this model, the Korea Foundation provides an endowment on an annual basis during the grant period for the establishment of a permanent professorship in Korean Studies or Korean Language.

However, the university must provide a matching fund contribution of 50% on a dollar-for-dollar basis.

In practical terms, universities considering this option must be prepared to contribute matching funds alongside the Korea Foundation’s support.

The endowed chair model is therefore particularly relevant to universities that have the financial capacity and institutional commitment to create a permanent academic position supported through an endowment structure.

Grant Duration

The grant period is expected to last between:

Three and five years.

The exact duration and conditions of support will be determined as part of the grant arrangement between the Korea Foundation and the selected university.

The university should therefore develop a clear multi-year plan that explains:

  • Why the professorship is needed
  • How it will be established
  • How it will contribute to Korean Studies or Korean language education
  • How the professor will be recruited
  • How the position will be integrated into the university
  • How the university will sustain the position
  • What outcomes are expected
  • How the program will contribute to the broader development of Korean Studies

What Happens After Korea Foundation Support Ends?

One of the defining characteristics of this opportunity is the emphasis on long-term sustainability.

The Korea Foundation wants to support universities that are capable of continuing the newly established professorship after the Foundation’s support concludes.

For a tenure-track position, the university is expected to maintain the position from its own resources.

For an endowed chair, the university participates in the creation of a jointly funded endowment.

This requirement means that applicants should have a realistic institutional strategy rather than relying entirely on Korea Foundation funding.

A strong application should therefore clearly explain how the professorship will remain financially and academically sustainable.

Requirements for the University

Universities seeking support should demonstrate that they have the necessary infrastructure and academic environment to support the development of Korean Studies or Korean language.

The institution should be able to demonstrate:

  • Existing interest in Korean Studies or Korean language
  • Appropriate academic infrastructure
  • Relevant faculty and academic activities
  • Suitable library resources
  • Relevant courses or programs
  • Institutional commitment to the proposed professorship
  • A long-term strategy for Korean Studies or Korean language development
  • Financial capacity to support the required institutional contribution
  • A credible plan for recruiting and retaining a qualified professor

The Korea Foundation will also consider whether the applicant university has the reputation, experience, and institutional capacity necessary to successfully implement the project.

Important Requirements for the Professor Who Will Hold the Position

Although the university is the applicant, the Korea Foundation also specifies important eligibility requirements for the person eventually appointed to the Korean Studies professorship.

The appointed professor must satisfy the following requirements.

1. More than 50% of research and teaching must focus on Korea

The professor’s research and teaching activities must have a focus on Korea in more than 50% of their overall academic work.

This means that the position is expected to be genuinely centered on Korean Studies rather than being a general academic position with only a minor Korean component.

2. Research must use Korean-language primary sources

The professor must conduct research using primary sources published in the Korean language.

This requirement demonstrates the Korea Foundation’s expectation that the professor will have the ability to engage directly with Korean-language academic and primary-source materials.

3. Research findings must be published in English

The professor is expected to publish research findings in English, with publication in Korean also potentially possible.

This helps ensure that research conducted through the supported professorship contributes to international academic discussions.

4. Korean-language proficiency

The professor must be proficient in the Korean language.

This is particularly important because the position requires direct engagement with Korean-language primary sources and the development of Korean Studies or Korean language education.

What Documents Are Required?

Applicants must submit an online application together with relevant supplementary materials.

The required documentation includes the following.

1. Online Application

The university must complete the Korea Foundation’s online application.

The application requires information about the institution’s current Korean Studies situation.

This includes information concerning areas such as:

  • Existing Korean Studies faculty
  • Existing Korean language faculty
  • Korean Studies courses
  • Korean language courses
  • Library collections
  • Academic activities
  • Existing programs
  • Institutional plans for Korean Studies development

Universities should therefore prepare detailed and accurate institutional information before beginning the application.

2. Curriculum for Korean Studies or Korean Language Degree Programs

Universities should provide the curriculum for their B.A. and/or M.A. programs in Korean Studies or Korean Language where applicable.

This document is required only if the university already offers degree programs in Korean Studies or Korean Language.

The curriculum can help demonstrate the university’s existing academic foundation and explain how the proposed professorship would fit into its academic structure.

3. University Professor Salary Scale

Applicants must provide information about the university’s salary scale for professors.

This is particularly relevant to the tenure-track model because the Korea Foundation’s support can cover up to 70% of the salary and employee benefits associated with the new position.

The salary information allows the Foundation to understand the financial structure of the proposed position.

4. Curriculum Vitae of the Professor to Be Hired

If the university already has a specific candidate in mind when submitting its application, it may provide that candidate’s curriculum vitae.

This document is only applicable where the institution has a concrete candidate at the time of application.

Having a candidate in mind can help demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed appointment, although the application requirements should be followed carefully regarding the recruitment and appointment process.

5. Curriculum Vitae of the Project Director

The university must provide the curriculum vitae of the person serving as the project director.

The project director will be responsible for overseeing the project and should therefore have an appropriate academic or institutional background.

The CV can help demonstrate the university’s ability to implement and manage the proposed project.

6. Letter from the Dean

Applicants must also submit a letter from the Dean of the faculty that plans to establish the Korean Studies professorship.

This provides evidence of faculty-level institutional support for the proposed position.

The letter should form part of the university’s broader demonstration of commitment to the establishment and long-term development of the professorship.

Language Requirements for the Application

All required application documents must be submitted in either:

  • Korean, or
  • English

Applications are submitted through the Korea Foundation Online Application System.

Universities should ensure that their supporting materials are properly prepared before submission and that all required information is included.

Application Deadline

The application period runs from:

July 1, 2026 to September 11, 2026.

Final deadline

September 11, 2026 at 18:00 KST

Applicants should pay close attention to the stated Korea Standard Time deadline.

Universities located in other time zones should convert the deadline to their local time and avoid waiting until the final hours to submit.

Because this is an institutional application requiring multiple supporting documents, universities should begin preparation well before the deadline.

Program Timeline

The Korea Foundation has provided the following schedule:

July 1, 2026

Application period opens.

September 11, 2026

Application period closes at 18:00 KST.

December 2026

Applicants are expected to receive notification of results.

2027-28 or 2028-29 Academic Year

The grant period is expected to commence during either the 2027-28 or 2028-29 academic year.

The actual commencement will depend on the outcome of the application and subsequent arrangements with the Korea Foundation.

How Applications Will Be Evaluated

The Korea Foundation will assess applications based on several important criteria.

1. Quality and Organization of the Proposed Plan

The Foundation will consider whether the proposal is sufficiently organized to achieve its stated objectives.

Applicants should therefore clearly explain:

  • What they want to establish
  • Why the professorship is necessary
  • How the position will be integrated into the university
  • What academic outcomes are expected
  • How the position will contribute to Korean Studies or Korean language education
  • How the university plans to sustain the position

The university should also demonstrate a clear institutional commitment to developing its Korean Studies or Korean language program.

2. Institutional Reputation and Previous Experience

The Foundation will consider the applicant university’s reputation and its previous accomplishments and experience in Korean Studies.

This means that applicants should clearly demonstrate existing strengths rather than simply stating that they are interested in Korea.

Evidence may include:

  • Existing Korean Studies courses
  • Existing Korean language courses
  • Faculty research
  • Academic publications
  • Conferences and seminars
  • Korean Studies events
  • Library resources
  • Research collaborations
  • Student enrollment
  • Existing academic programs

The university’s track record can help demonstrate its capacity to successfully implement the proposed project.

3. Quality of the Budget Plan

The budget is another major evaluation factor.

The Korea Foundation will assess whether the proposed budget is:

  • Sound
  • Specific
  • Realistic
  • Properly justified
  • Consistent with the proposed project

The Foundation will also consider the applicant university’s matching-fund effort where applicable.

Universities applying for an endowed chair should pay particular attention to the matching-fund requirement.

A poorly explained budget could weaken an otherwise strong application.

4. Feasibility and Expected Outcomes

Applicants must demonstrate that their proposed objectives are realistic and achievable.

The Foundation will assess:

  • Whether the university can successfully implement the project
  • Whether the proposed professorship is genuinely needed
  • Whether the expected academic outcomes are realistic
  • How the position will contribute to Korean Studies
  • How the project can support the diversification of Korean Studies across different regions

The regional dimension is particularly important because the program seeks to contribute to the broader international development and diversification of Korean Studies.

Long-Term Institutional Commitment

The Korea Foundation expects recipient universities to demonstrate a strong long-term commitment to the professorship.

The university should not treat the grant as a temporary project that ends when Korea Foundation funding ends.

Instead, the institution should establish a sustainable structure through either:

  • Continued institutional funding for a tenure-track position; or
  • A jointly established endowment for an endowed chair.

This makes long-term planning one of the most important components of a competitive application.

Fair Appointment and Promotion Requirements

The recipient university must ensure that the person holding the professorship is appointed and promoted through a thorough and fair review of their qualifications and accomplishments.

The process should comply with the university’s established procedures for:

  • Faculty appointment
  • Promotion
  • Tenure
  • Academic evaluation

The Korea Foundation therefore expects the recruitment and career progression of the professor to follow appropriate institutional standards rather than being based solely on informal selection.

Important Conditions Applicants Should Know

There are several important conditions attached to the program.

Cancellation of Support

The Korea Foundation may cancel its support decision if the Foundation and the recipient university are unable to conclude the required grant agreement.

Being selected for support therefore does not mean that funding is automatically disbursed without further arrangements.

Notification of Changes

The applicant university must promptly notify the Korea Foundation about significant changes to the approved project.

This includes changes such as:

  • Postponement
  • Cancellation
  • Changes to the project plan
  • Other significant modifications

Universities should therefore maintain communication with the Foundation throughout the project.

Revision of the Project Plan

The Korea Foundation may request an applicant institution to revise its project plan or add new elements if the Foundation considers this necessary.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to make reasonable adjustments during the review or agreement process.

How Grant Funds Are Disbursed

Before grant funding is made available, the Korea Foundation and the selected university must enter into a grant agreement.

The agreement will contain details relating to:

  • The project
  • The budget
  • Funding arrangements
  • Responsibilities of both parties
  • Other agreed conditions

The final project and budget will be determined through discussions between the Korea Foundation and the recipient university.

For a tenure-track position specifically, the Korea Foundation’s salary and employee-benefit support will be provided after the grant agreement has been concluded and the recipient university has employed a qualified candidate for the position.

This is an important distinction for universities when planning their recruitment and financial arrangements.

Annual Reporting Requirements

Recipient universities must submit an annual project report to the Korea Foundation during the term of the agreement.

The annual report must also include a financial statement.

The financial statement must be:

  • Prepared by the university’s accounting officer
  • Signed by the accounting officer
  • Submitted according to the Foundation’s reporting requirements

The Korea Foundation will provide the relevant reporting form.

Universities should therefore maintain accurate financial and project records throughout the grant period.

Why This Opportunity Is Significant

The establishment of a permanent Korean Studies or Korean Language professorship can have a substantial impact on a university’s academic community.

A new professorship can help an institution:

  • Expand its Korean Studies curriculum
  • Increase Korean language teaching capacity
  • Develop new academic courses
  • Strengthen research on Korea
  • Recruit students interested in Korea
  • Increase academic publications
  • Build international research partnerships
  • Organize seminars and conferences
  • Develop Korean Studies expertise in its region
  • Create opportunities for students to engage with Korean language and society
  • Strengthen the university’s international academic profile

The opportunity can be particularly valuable for universities that already have some Korean Studies activities but need additional faculty capacity to expand them into a more comprehensive academic program.

What Makes a Strong Application?

Although the Korea Foundation will make the final assessment, universities can strengthen their applications by developing a clear and evidence-based proposal.

A strong proposal should clearly answer several questions.

Why does the university need a new Korean Studies or Korean Language professor?

The application should demonstrate a genuine academic need.

What existing infrastructure does the university have?

Applicants should explain their current courses, faculty, library resources, student interest, research activities, and other relevant assets.

What will the new professor actually accomplish?

The university should present measurable and realistic academic objectives.

How will the university sustain the position?

This is especially important because of the program’s emphasis on long-term sustainability.

How will the position contribute to regional Korean Studies?

Applicants should explain how the professorship will contribute beyond the university itself and support the broader development of Korean Studies in its region.

Is the budget realistic?

Every major financial component should be clearly justified.

Who Is This Opportunity Best Suited For?

This opportunity is best suited to universities that already have an academic foundation in Korean Studies or Korean language and want to significantly expand that capacity.

It may be particularly relevant to institutions that:

  • Already teach Korean language
  • Offer Korean Studies courses
  • Have faculty conducting research on Korea
  • Have Korean Studies library resources
  • Have students interested in Korea
  • Want to establish a permanent academic position
  • Have a long-term plan for Korean Studies
  • Can provide the necessary institutional funding or matching contribution
  • Have sufficient administrative capacity to manage a multi-year grant

Universities without any meaningful infrastructure or institutional commitment to Korean Studies may find it more difficult to demonstrate the capacity required under the evaluation criteria.

Application Process

Universities interested in applying should follow the official Korea Foundation application process.

The general process involves:

  1. Reviewing the program requirements carefully.
  2. Determining whether the university plans to establish a new Korean Studies or Korean Language professorship.
  3. Assessing the university’s existing Korean Studies infrastructure.
  4. Developing the proposed professorship plan.
  5. Determining whether the institution will pursue the tenure-track or endowed chair model.
  6. Preparing the relevant financial information.
  7. Preparing the required supporting documents.
  8. Obtaining the necessary institutional and faculty-level approvals.
  9. Completing the online application.
  10. Uploading the required supplementary materials.
  11. Submitting the application before the deadline.
  12. Awaiting the Korea Foundation’s decision in December 2026.

Applications and required documentation should be submitted through the Korea Foundation Online Application System.

Official Application and Contact Information

Applications are submitted through the Korea Foundation Online Application System.

More information visit HERE

More global opportunities visit the OFY Website HERE

Program-related questions can be directed to:

Email: studies@kf.or.kr

Technical questions relating to the Korea Foundation Online Application System can be directed to:

Email: tech-support@kf.or.kr

Applicants are advised to use Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge when working with the online application system. The announcement states that Internet Explorer and Safari are not supported for stable document work.

Final Deadline Reminder

The application deadline is:

September 11, 2026 at 18:00 KST

Universities should not wait until the deadline to begin preparing their applications. The required materials can involve information from multiple university departments, including academic faculties, finance or administration offices, and institutional leadership.

Early preparation can therefore give applicants enough time to develop a strong proposal, verify salary information, prepare supporting documents, obtain the Dean’s letter, review the budget, and complete the online application properly.

Conclusion

The 2027 Korea Foundation Support for Establishment of Professorship represents a significant opportunity for universities outside Korea seeking to strengthen and institutionalize their academic work in Korean Studies or Korean Language.

Rather than functioning as an individual scholarship or short-term research grant, the program is designed to help universities create new, sustainable professorships that can contribute to the long-term development of Korean Studies.

Selected institutions may receive substantial financial support through either a tenure-track model, where the Korea Foundation can provide up to 70% of salary and employee benefits, or an endowed chair model involving an annual endowment and a 50% dollar-for-dollar matching contribution from the university.

However, financial support is only one part of the opportunity. Successful applicants must demonstrate institutional capacity, a strong academic foundation, realistic objectives, a sound budget, long-term sustainability, and a genuine commitment to developing Korean Studies or Korean language education.

The application period is open from July 1 to September 11, 2026, with the final deadline at 18:00 KST on September 11, 2026. Results are scheduled to be announced in December 2026, while supported projects are expected to begin during either the 2027-28 or 2028-29 academic year.

Universities interested in expanding their Korean Studies or Korean language programs should carefully review the eligibility requirements, prepare the necessary institutional documentation, develop a strong and sustainable project plan, and submit their application through the Korea Foundation’s official online application system before the deadline.
